claim: moment.py's contiguity signature is CONFIRMED still not a real pre-registered test -- the audit's 'cannot fail while _DRIFT<1' verdict holds, verified two ways. (1) Code read: status() (core/moment.py lines 300-318) computes contiguity_gap = cos(adjacent keys) - cos(distant keys), where key is produced by _drift_key() (lines 46-50), an exponential moving average with weight _DRIFT=0.12 on new content and 0.88 retained from the previous key, L2-normalized. This is a smoothing/AR(1)-style recursion on the unit sphere -- adjacent-lag autocorrelation exceeds distant-lag autocorrelation as a property of the recursion itself, independent of whether the underlying thought content has any genuine temporal/associative relationship. (2) Empirical null-model test: fed the SAME _drift_key() recursion pure random 40-char garbage strings (no semantic or temporal relationship between successive 'thoughts' at all) for every tested _DRIFT value from 0.05 to 0.95, and contiguity_gap came out POSITIVE every time (0.024 to 0.930 depending on DRIFT), with zero real content structure driving it. This directly demonstrates the signature is a mathematical artifact of the EMA recursion, not evidence of a real contiguity effect, exactly as the audit found. Live status() on the current 14,201-row moments.jsonl (up from 13,011 at audit time) still reports contiguity_gap=+0.14 (adjacent=0.994, distant=0.854), consistent with the plan's own cited +0.154 and the audit's +0.98 (different windows). This plan should keep counting moment.py's read-path evidence as UNVALIDATED (write-only, per audit) until a real pre-registered test replaces contiguity_gap -- e.g. a null-model comparison (shuffle thought order, recompute gap, require the real-order gap to beat the shuffled distribution) or dropping the EMA key in favor of directly comparing real semantic content between temporally-adjacent vs distant moments.

claim: J-0178: merge_threshold cannot be safely raised toward the plan's 'a handful (~4-8)' target on the current guidance_beliefs.json corpus (154 principles, 2026-08-24) without producing genuinely incoherent parent-value merges (contradictory beliefs forced under one medoid) -- live seed() defaults (threshold=0.46, merge_threshold=0.6) left UNCHANGED. Swept 21 (online_threshold, merge_threshold) combos in an isolated copy via _cluster_values() called directly on the real guidance_beliefs.json corpus. Two independent findings: (1) merge_threshold (the agglomerative second pass) is INERT across the entire realistic range tested (0.40-0.72) -- identical parent counts/sizes at every merge_threshold for a fixed online threshold, because after the online pass no two cluster centroids ever reach even 0.6 cosine similarity; only the ONLINE threshold moves parent count. (2) Lowering the online threshold enough to approach the plan's 8-12 or 4-8 target (threshold<=0.40) produces parents that fail the briefing's own coherence bar -- eyeballed the actual children lists, not just counts. At threshold=0.40 (18 parents) one 20-member parent's medoid is 'True understanding comes from recognizing that external labels...are just descriptions of an underlying reality' yet its own children include a directly contradictory member, 'Objective truths, like the cleanliness of water, exist independently of our feelings or desires, and we must rely on verifiable methods' -- an objectivist-empiricist stance merged into a constructivist/subjectivist medoid, i.e. NOT one real belief. At threshold=0.36 (11 parents, inside target band) this worsens: 48 of 154 beliefs collapse into a single 'Learning/Understanding' parent spanning narrative identity, presence/acceptance, objective-truth claims, and self-construction theories -- a forced blend, not a coherent value. Additionally the online/greedy algorithm is non-monotonic and order-sensitive near the current regime: threshold 0.42->19 parents, 0.43->26, 0.44->25, 0.45->27, 0.46->27 -- small threshold changes jump unpredictably, so there is no stable dial between '26-27 coherent-but-fine-grained' and '8-12 with real contradiction-merges'; no tested value satisfies both the plan's count target and the briefing's per-parent coherence requirement. Verdict: leave live seed() untouched; the plan's Section 7 'a handful' language is not achievable via this cosine+medoid mechanism on this corpus without sacrificing coherence -- a founder call is needed on whether to accept ~26 parents as the practical floor, invest in a smarter clustering approach (e.g. contradiction-aware splitting, LLM-assisted topic grouping), or revise the plan's target language. claim: SOTA research on cascaded compression and per-band/per-subspace indexing: (1) cascading compression stages that each target a different redundancy class (positional/predictive, then spatial-frequency transform, then statistical entropy coding) is exactly how every modern media codec already works -- AV1, HEVC, G-PCC point-cloud compression, JPEG2000 all follow this structure, decades-old validated production practice. (2) Per-band differentiated processing (different quantization/bit-allocation/treatment per frequency band based on that band's own statistics) is the FOUNDING principle of subband coding -- MPEG audio's psychoacoustic per-subband bit allocation (1990s) and JPEG2000's per-subband quantization are the canonical, standardized, shipped-in-billions-of-devices examples. (3) Heterogeneous index types chosen per column/subspace within one system (B-tree/GiST/GIN/HNSW coexisting in Postgres, polystore/multi-model databases like BigDAWG) is also well-established mainstream practice. HOWEVER: the specific combination this project is designing -- a DISTINCT INDEX STRUCTURE (not just quantization rule) per FDM-style band carved out of ONE multiplexed/compressed stream -- has no direct precedent found in the literature. Each ingredient is proven; this specific recipe (cascaded-redundancy compression + FDM band-splitting + a distinct index structure per band) appears to be a genuinely novel combination, not something already tried and reported
evidence: Agent research session 2026-08-24. Citations: AV1 technical overview arXiv:2008.06091; G-PCC/LiDAR compression survey ACM TOMM 2025 dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715916; JPEG2000 technical overviews (McMaster ECE, IIT Bombay course notes) explicitly stating wavelet transform restructures but does not itself compress -- entropy coding does; Shannon source coding theorem as the entropy floor; BigDAWG polystore arXiv:1609.07548; Lu and Holubova multi-model database survey ACM Computing Surveys 2019; PostgreSQL index-types docs (B-tree/GiST/GIN/BRIN/hash per column); pgvector HNSW-alongside-classic-indexes production pattern; Peter Noll MPEG Digital Audio Coding Standards (per-subband psychoacoustic bit allocation). ROOT CAUSE 1: the harnesses backed up and restored the .db and its -wal as SEPARATE file copies; restoring a mismatched pair makes SQLite replay the wrong journal on next open, destroying the main file (its header was raw page data, not 'SQLite format 3'). One harness's -shm restore had even errored visibly ('user-mapped section open') and I noted it as harmless -- it was the symptom. ROOT CAUSE 2 (turned the first fix attempt into a second corruption): hud/server.py holds a READ-ONLY sqlite connection to the same file continuously (server.py:1243, mode=ro), so my copy landed on an open file; a read-only WAL connection still maps the file and pins -wal/-shm. LESSONS, binding for any future harness: (1) never file-copy a WAL-mode sqlite db -- use sqlite3's backup API or checkpoint first, one file, no siblings; (2) never restore while ANY process holds the file, including read-only holders like the HUD; (3) a failed sibling-file restore is an integrity failure, not a warning to shrug off.

claim: Given F-1345's mechanism read, the peer_reflection recall gate reads as plausibly mistuned relative to Item 1's own stated design intent, not as an intentional-conservative design where near-total silence is simply the expected, healthy outcome. social_world_school.md's Item 1 Approach describes the intended mechanism as a fragment that "competes with every other fragment for relevance... returns quietly when nothing connects... competes on equal footing" -- ordinary bounded relevance-gating where occasional silence (G7's own criterion) is expected and fine. What F-1345 found instead is not that kind of occasional, evenly-distributed silence: it is a specific, near-total (15/15 observed) structural crowding-out of peer_reflection by its own closest topical rival -- that same peer's raw letter thread -- in the one scenario (a new letter to/from that peer) the design doc itself names as the primary real trigger for this origin to ever surface. A design built to let a peer's distilled understanding occasionally colour a reply is, as currently tuned, effectively unable to do so in the most relevant moment it was built for, and an additional 29% of the corpus ages into an even-harder-to-reach cold tier within about two weeks, well inside typical peer correspondence cadence. This reads as the class of "mistuned" the job's own briefing asked to distinguish from working-as-intended, though it remains this job's own characterization of verified facts, not a certainty about the original design's intent, and is offered as the job's briefing explicitly requested.
evidence:
social_world_school.md, Item 1 "Read-path / actuation (how it reaches behaviour) -- REVISED" section (the live, current design, not the struck-through original): "embedding-similarity-gated..., competes with every other fragment for relevance, returns quietly when nothing connects...", and "a peer_reflection fragment surfaces only if it's actually relevant to that content... If nothing connects, nothing surfaces -- same as any other memory. This is the G6 fix: the reflection is offered through the same channel as any recollection, competing on equal footing, never a command prepended ahead of generation." Verification section explicitly anticipates "recall_fragments/recall_block's logging shows non-zero, non-constant surfacing (proof it's relevance-gated, not silently dead)" as the healthy outcome, and separately names the Phase 0 watch-item "does anything ever actually recall" as a real risk to check for, not dismiss.

F-1345 (this job, same session) found the observed behaviour does not match "competing on equal footing" for the realistic case: 15/15 real production-code tests using real peer letters as the query surfaced zero peer_reflection fragments, with the same-peer's own raw letter thread (origin='peer') winning 2-6 of the top-6 trail slots every single time -- a specific, identifiable, near-total (not merely biased) crowding-out, not a fragment quietly failing to connect roughly half the time as ordinary relevance-gating with real content would be expected to produce. This is why the read leans "mistuned" rather than "by design": the plan's own design language anticipates fair, occasional non-surfacing, and what was measured is closer to structural exclusion in the primary intended trigger scenario.

Caveat, stated plainly: this is this job's own interpretive judgment applied to F-1345's verified facts, offered because the job briefing explicitly asked for a mistuned-vs-by-design characterization -- it is not a claim that the original 2026-08-24 design (J-0129/D-0016) intended this outcome, nor a claim about what fix (if any) the founder should choose. It does not touch D-0016/D-0178 (per this job's own briefing): the observed problem is under-surfacing/silence, not a reflection ever functioning as an unchallenged directive (over-surfacing/steering) -- D-0016/D-0178's own shared defeater is about the latter, which this finding does not report evidence of either way.

The 78 total "[locomotion] WATCHDOG completed a stuck journey" lines in data/nascence.log's whole
history (2026-08-25 through the log's real end 2026-09-13 09:08:40 -- not just F-1397's own 09-11/13

journey was still in-flight in data/position.json when the process was last stopped, and the first
locomotion.tick() after the next boot finds it long past _WATCHDOG_S and force-completes it. This is
exactly what core/locomotion.py's own module docstring documents by design ("survives restarts -- a
journey older than its watchdog window COMPLETES with a log line naming it: instruments must say
why"). Fully benign, working as intended, not a bug.

(B) The other 63 hits (100% to study, zero exceptions) are a real, live, worsening bug distinct from
(A): core/night.py's to_bed() begins a real multi-leg locomotion journey to study as literally the
first action of every sleep cycle (called from nodes/inner_monologue_node.py's _enter_sleep(), before
state["asleep"]=True is even set), and that journey -- whose own legs take only 20-90s -- then sits
completely un-ticked for the WHOLE span until _enter_sleep()'s own multi-stage LLM pipeline (chapter
formation, journal, world-pass/consolidation, downscale, dream) finally finishes and yields control
back. This span has grown, in lockstep, on two independent measures: the watchdog's own "started Ns
ago" values (900-950s in late August climbing smoothly to 1500s+ by 09-12/13) and data/night_log.jsonl's
own independently-recorded pipeline-stage timings (total sleep duration_s ~1700-2500s in late August vs
routinely 2800-5400s by 09-09/09-12). Daily frequency shows the same step-change: 0-2 mid-session hits
a day before 2026-09-06, then 7-9 a day from 09-06 onward -- now matching or exceeding that day's total
logged sleep-cycle count, i.e. the watchdog has stopped being a rare safety net and become the NORMAL
path for a sleep-onset journey, not an edge case.

This is NOT a fully benign, by-design consequence of ordinary tick cadence, for two evidenced reasons:
(1) it is no longer rare and is still worsening, and (2) for the whole un-ticked span,
core/sensorium.py's own move()/begin_journey() path deliberatly leaves state["location"] reporting

one. Left, honestly, for the spawned follow-up job rather than guessed at here.

3. GROUND TRUTH: ran the real core.literal_will.classify(thought, intention, act_kind=..., act_object=...) over every row (both files), using each row's own real intention/act_kind/act_object fields, and kept only readings where verdict=="DEED", family is a real dispatchable hand (gated=True, binds!=''), and the winning clause has an (he|she|they|travis|darwin|marcus|smith) subject immediately followed by that same family's own verb (in some inflected form) NOT already in _B_OTHER's covered base list (light/lay/stoke/feed/gather/make/brew/water/sow/write/tend/put/set/take/hang/pull/blow/turn).

Root cause: a VERB/NOUN HOMONYM COLLISION, not a missing common deed verb -- "saw" is simultaneously (i) the woodwork family's own cutting-verb, (ii) the woodwork family's own tool-OBJECT (a hand saw), and (iii) the ordinary irregular past tense of "to see". classify()'s pronoun-carry branch ("verb + it/them/one/back/him/her", present_objs non-empty) matches "he saw them" directly: "saw" satisfies the verb regex, and the very same literal "saw" token also satisfies present_objs (the tool-object list), so deed_grammar fires True with zero real woodworking content in the sentence.

"they get ... spring" satisfies deed_grammar's verb-reaches-object branch (no comma/semicolon between them), and the other-person subject "they get" is not caught because "get" is not in _B_OTHER's list.

claim:
J-0886 side-finding bearing on any D-0185 'option c' revisit: memory-levels gisting cannot retire the existing backlog at any cap setting, because shadow_distill only ever looks at raw rows NEWER than a moving frontier (data/memory_levels_shadow_state.json last_ts) - so raising _KIND_BUCKET_CAP / _MAX_CLUSTERS / MAX_DEMOTE_PER_RUN alone can slow the growth of semantic/self active_total, but can never shrink it back to the K x keep_kind budgets.

Mechanism (code read in full, core/memory_levels.py lines 91-103, 512-522, 529-534, 602): the fetch is `WHERE abstraction_level = 0 AND cold = 0 AND timestamp > <last_ts> AND origin IN (eligible) ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 160`, and at the end of every run that formed >=1 cluster `_set_last_ts(newest_ts)` moves the frontier to the newest timestamp among ALL clustered source rows. A warm raw row at or below the frontier is never fetched again (a reset of the state file would only re-expose the newest 160 rows per run, not walk the backlog - there is no cursor). Fact check on the live store at 2026-09-19 11:45 (DB mode=ro; frontier last_ts = 2026-09-19 01:44:11 from the state file): warm (cold=0) level-0 eligible-origin rows - semantic (reading/study/research) 13,654 of which 13,481 (98.7%) lie at/below the frontier and only 173 above it; self (subconscious_synthesis/inner_thought/seed) 12,787 of which 12,337 (96.5%) at/below, 450 above; episodic (lived) 2,674 of which 2,652 (99.2%) at/below, 22 above. So 98.7% / 96.5% of the two kinds whose growth D-0185/D-0183 are about are structurally out of reach of this pipeline; only newly arriving intake is ever gisted, and only the newest slice of it (see the separate inferred finding on the 160-row window).

Consequence for the defeater arithmetic: memory-levels can at best offset a fraction of NEW intake (today 20.5% of self, 8.5% of semantic per live-day, see F-1580); the standing 13.7k/12.9k backlogs would need a different mechanism (a backlog sweep with a cursor, the D-0124/D-0173 hard-backstop option (b), or a keep/budget decision - D-0183) regardless of how the throughput caps are set. Not a bug: the frontier is what makes each run cheap and non-repeating; it is simply a property the D-0185 sizing (J-0690, which treated _FETCH_LIMIT as affecting quality not throughput under the old one-bucket-per-kind rule) did not carry forward to the multi-bucket regime.

claim:
J-0886 side-finding (INFERRED - rests on an estimated fetch time): in the multi-bucket regime the _FETCH_LIMIT=160 window per run appears to be a second real throughput ceiling: an estimated 35-40% of the 48 post-merge runs had more new eligible raw rows waiting than the 160 the fetch can take, and because the frontier then jumps to the newest clustered row, roughly half of all NEW eligible intake is never examined by memory-levels at all.

Method: for each post-merge run k, frontier F_k = newest timestamp among the source rows of its logged clusters (source_ids looked up in the DB); the pool visible to run k = level-0 rows with origin in the seven eligible origins and F_(k-1) < timestamp <= (first shadow row ts of run k - 90 s), the -90 s being my estimate of when the fetch happened relative to the first cluster's row being written. Results over the 48 runs: pool per run mean 308, median 148, min 90, max 956 (upper bound counting all such rows; a lower bound counting only rows that are cold=0 today gives mean 253, median 102, and undercounts because the rows gisted are cold now). Runs with pool > 160: 19 of 48 by the upper bound, 17 of 48 by the lower bound (35-40%). Histogram of pool sizes (bins of 50): 50-99: 7 runs, 100-149: 17, 150-199: 7, 200-249: 2, 300-349: 2, >=400: 13 (the big pools are the first run after each restart and runs after long reading bursts). In steady-state runs (pool < 500, n=35) mean pool 140 and only 4-6 exceed 160. Totals over the 48 runs: 14,794 new eligible rows entered the pool (the DB shows 14,659 eligible level-0 rows created in the window, consistent), of which at most 6,521 (44.1%) fit the newest-160 window, 3,600 (24.3%) were placed in a cluster (75.0 per run), and 2,156 (14.6%) were retired behind a committed gist. Rows beyond the 160 window that were never re-fetchable: 7,083 (lower bound) to 8,273 (upper bound), i.e. 48-56% of new intake.

Reading (inference, not measurement): at the current cadence (7.55 runs/live-day) the window caps rows examined at ~1,200/live-day against ~2,300/live-day eligible intake, so even an unlimited bucket cap and MAX_DEMOTE_PER_RUN could not reach intake parity without also raising _FETCH_LIMIT and/or run cadence. The bucket caps bind too (self hit its 5 in 26/48 runs, semantic in 21/48), so the ceilings stack: fetch window, bucket caps, semantic faithfulness (see F-1580's arithmetic and the semantic finding), and the demote cap. Uncertainty to close before relying on the size of the effect: the fetch-time estimate, and rows already cold for other reasons at fetch time (bounded by the lower/upper pair above). A precise version needs the per-run pool logged at fetch time (a one-line observe-only log in shadow_distill), which does not exist today.

claim: J-0639 item (3): the 90-second OBSERVE_COOLDOWN drops most of Du's thoughts before they ever reach the pursuit register, which corroborates and sharpens F-0768's ~40% register-coverage estimate. MEASURED: the cooldown_skip_unresolved instrument logged 1,734 rows in 171.1 live hours = 10.1 per live hour (ceiling 40/h at one row per 90-s window; the minimum gap between consecutive rows is 90.0 s and none is shorter), each row being ONE 90-s window that contained at least one dropped unresolved thought, so the row count undercounts lost thoughts. F-0768's own metric recomputed on the post-restart days: per-observe register events (born 155 + advance_pending 2,796 + restated 131 = 3,082) divided by the 7,273 monologue thoughts of >=25 characters in data/monologue_log.jsonl = 42.4% (daily range 38.4-52.0%), against F-0768's 413/1,053 = 39.2% (09-02) and 423/1,077 = 39.3% (09-03) -- the same coverage, not a regression. Cadence: the median gap between consecutive thoughts is 49 s and 92.6% of gaps are under 90 s, so a 90-s cooldown structurally passes about two of every five thoughts. MODEL-DERIVED (validated, but a model): simulating the cooldown over the monologue stream (observe runs only if >=90 s have passed since the last observed thought) yields 3,096 observed thoughts against the 3,082 actual per-observe events (0.5% off) and 1,739 rate-limited skip windows against the 1,734 actual cooldown_skip rows (0.3% off), so the simulation reproduces both independent counts. On it, of the 4,132 unresolved thoughts of >=25 characters in the window ~1,758 (42.5%) were observed and ~2,374 (57.5%, about 13.9 per live hour) were lost to the cooldown (daily 47-61%); the 155 births are 8.8% of the observed unresolved thoughts. The 渡 case F-0768 started from: 407 of the 7,273 thoughts (5.6%) mention 渡 in text or about-label; 233 (57%) were cooldown-skipped; of the 174 observed, 141 (81%) matched an ACTIVE pursuit (advance_pending, so a reawaken rule never sees them), 22 reached the else-branch with no event (max cosine to every dormant below 0.55), 9 produced a reawaken_candidate (3 candidate-only, 6 alongside a birth) and 2 produced a birth only. Consequence for the briefing's item (4): the cooldown, not terminal dormancy, is the larger loss on concept threads like 渡 (57% of them never observed), and it is a separate lever from re-awakening.

claim: J-0639 item (4), characterization (my inference from F-1597/F-1599 plus a small hand read): the shadow rows show a re-awaken path would fire often, but they do not show that its matches are real continuations, so promoting one (dormant to active, heat = HEAT_BORN, thought queued advance_pending, birth suppressed) is NOT yet warranted by this data and no decision should be opened on it yet; what is needed first is a decoupled-judge quality read of a candidate sample. BASIS. (a) Volume is real: 1.33 candidates per live hour, and 83% of the window's births (129/155) duplicate a dormant thread within cosine >=0.55. But the cosine signal is weak (median 0.66 against the 0.55 bar; non-templated median 0.65) and about 30% of rows are the templated reading-log sentences, where an exact-1.0 match is the same auto-generated sentence repeating and 'I finished a book - and reached for something new: <book>' matches across DIFFERENT books at 0.82-0.89 (false continuity). (b) The rare-token second signal, computed text-only (no cosine bar) between each of the ~519 observed thoughts that reached the else-branch and the question/about of the CURRENT register's 466 dormant pursuits (register-at-thought-time not reconstructed, so approximate): it would flag 185 thoughts (35.6%), each hitting a median of 21 dormant pursuits, dominated by 'Travis' (78 thoughts) and the ideogram 渡 (22), then book-title words -- it identifies a FAMILY (21 dormant pursuits mention 渡), not the specific thread, so it can only be a ranker or filter alongside cosine, never a rule by itself. Its concept-level catch is real but narrow: 22 else-branch 渡 thoughts share the ideogram with a dormant 渡 pursuit, against the 2 CJK-overlap rows the cosine-gated instrument logged -- so F-0768's question is answered yes for 渡 (the token would have caught what cosine missed), but that is ~22 thoughts in 7.1 live days, while 57% of 渡 thoughts never reach observe() (cooldown) and 81% of the observed ones are swallowed by an active pursuit before the reawaken scan runs (F-1599). (c) My own hand read of 20 stratified candidate pairs (thought vs the dormant pursuit's own question; a single reader, not a decoupled judge, so indicative only): 11 are templated reading-log (8 same-book re-openings or exact repeats, real but mechanical; 3 generic 'finished a book' matches across different books, false), and of the 9 concept-level pairs 7 look like plausible thread or motif recurrence (cat/spiral 0.82, arithmetic 0.69, invisible economic forces 0.72, thyme and sea 0.69, cat-naming/garden 0.75, climb to the garden 0.61, chest/knot 0.64) and 2 look weak (beetle vs dust motes 0.61, dream/markets vs dream's winged cat 0.58); 'plausible' still cannot tell accumulation from Du's few recurring motifs (the tour-not-build failure the plan already measures). CONSTRAINTS any promotion would need (design notes, not a build): exclude or handle the reading-log templates separately (23.2% of births, 29.8% of candidate rows); use cosine as the ranker with the token overlap as a specificity boost and require a cross-family judge confirmation before status changes (the plan's decoupled-judge law, as pending advances already do); treat the 90-s cooldown as the larger lever; and note CAP=4 competition (3 active now, 466 dormant) and D-0109's serial-RETURN ruling (a revived dormant pursuit re-enters the return-eligible pool, changing its composition). Recommended next step: a decoupled-judge read of >=60 candidate rows stratified by cosine band and by templated/non-templated, reporting the continuation yes-rate per band; a follow-up job is spawned for it.

J-0662 mechanism (INFERRED; companion to F-1604): the stream_drive 'ignition' column is the max of TWO independent reservoir sawtooths (plus a protoself-drive term), so a fire's post-fire drop is (1 - the OTHER reservoir's level). F-0947's five shrinking drops were the slow defensive reservoir charging beneath the fast exploratory 42.1-minute metronome, a within-cycle pattern that resets at every defensive fire, and 'the pre-fire peak pinned near the 1.0 clip' is the fire condition itself, not a measurement of saturation. CODE (core/climate_engine.py, read this session). ignition_level() = max(dissonance.value, dissonance.explore_value) / _IGNITION_THRESHOLD (1.0), clipped to [0,1]; _ignite() zeroes ONLY the reservoir that fired (defensive: value=0; exploratory: explore_value=0); 300 s refractory after any fire; defensive has priority when both are ready. core/stream_drive._ignition() then takes max(ignition_level(), 1 - exp(-protoself drive)). A fire happens when a reservoir reaches 1.0, so the reading just before it is about 1.0 by construction, and the reading just after it is the other reservoir's level (or the protoself term if higher).

DATA. (a) Fill times, live minutes between consecutive same-type fires: exploratory median 42.1 in EVERY era (p10 42.0; P0 n=106, A1 30, A2 116, A3 91) = a metronome (1/0.0004 s^-1 = 41.7 min plus tick); defensive median 180.5 in P0 (n=19, p10 139, p90 404), then 46.4 (A1), 52.3 (A2), 40.4 (A3) after option A. WHAT CHANGED (one source file, one new test; base 5a66504). The body of find_cluster became the generator _find_cluster_steps(level), which yields once per SEED_SCAN_BLOCK = 4096 pairs of the all-pairs seed scan. find_cluster(level) (same signature, synchronous) drives it straight through. New find_cluster_async(level) drives it and awaits asyncio.sleep(0) at every yield. try_form_chapter now does 'await find_cluster_async(lv)' (its only edit). The only edit inside the algorithm: the per-row neighbour count is taken block by block (the same integer) with a yield between blocks; the strict 'n > best_n' first-maximum-wins rule, the per-pair predicate, every statement after the seed loop, _candidates/_cooled/_era_window and every constant are AST-identical to the base. WHY NOT asyncio.to_thread (measured). A worker thread passes the plain 50 ms heartbeat (worst tick lag 41 ms) but np.dot drops the GIL on every call, so a loop callback that does GIL-releasing work (sqlite / file / log calls, i.e. what a substrate tick does) runs 100-2,000x slower while the worker scans: a callback of 20 sqlite calls has median 0.06 ms idle, 0.05 ms with the coroutine scan and 85-146 ms with a worker thread (worst 200-460 ms). A worker thread also cannot be cancelled (a cancelled sleep leaves a 25-minute orphan scan and the next call starts a second one) and holds process exit hostage (measured: the awaiting task cancelled and main() returned at 0.2 s, asyncio.run returned at 6.0 s = the worker's length).

RESULTS. (a) Heartbeat, n=1,300 (a 1.8 s scan): the blocking call as today gives a worst tick lag of 1,781-1,851 ms (5 runs) and 12 ticks; find_cluster_async gives 15.7-16.4 ms (Windows timer granularity) and 46 ticks. At production block geometry (n=6,000, two 4,096-pair blocks per row): worst 26.8 ms over 729 ticks and a GIL-releasing callback median 0.050 ms. One 4,096-pair block is 4.3-4.7 ms. (b) Equivalence: output identical (order included) to a frozen verbatim copy of the base find_cluster, with identical pre-era membership (the timestamps handed to _era_window), on clustered synthetic data with 120 decoy rows (chapter_id set / other origin / no embedding / younger than 48 h), exact ties (first maximum wins: 200-vs-200 A first, 200-vs-200 B first, 200-vs-201), 300 pairs within +-3e-7 of CLUSTER_SIM (146 pass in float32, independent per-pair recount equal), levels 1 and 2, boundary sizes (0, 39, 40 rows) and 2,400 REAL rows (pre-era cluster 58, era rule 24 members; base 6.3 s vs async 6.3 s); also equal to an independent float64 matrix oracle. So the sleep length is unchanged. (d) Cancellation reaches the scan 0.3-0.7 ms after cancel() (next yield), nothing keeps scanning, the flag is released and a following call runs one clean scan; an overlapping call never starts a second scan; the exception path releases the flag; try_form_chapter never calls the blocking find_cluster and calls its author only after the scan has finished, with the loop ticking through (21 ticks, worst 15-16 ms).

THREAD-SAFETY READING (find_cluster read end to end; it matters only because no thread is used): _connect() opens a NEW sqlite connection on every call (no module-global connection, cursor or cache), the function is read-only (one SELECT), _blob_to_vec is np.frombuffer over the row's own bytes, _cosine is float(np.dot), the module globals it reads are constants and pure helpers, logging is thread-safe. float32 np.dot on 384-dim vectors is bit-identical across buffer alignments (0..60 bytes) and between a worker thread and the main thread (4,400 pairs incl. 400 within 5e-7 of 0.70), so even a thread could not have flipped a threshold pair. The only shared mutable state this change adds is _SCANNING, touched from the loop thread only.

claim: LESSON for every future 'move it off the event loop' change in Nascence (found while building J-1180): asyncio.to_thread / a worker thread is NOT a free way to un-freeze the loop when the loop's own callbacks do GIL-releasing work. A worker thread that runs numpy in a tight Python loop passes the plain heartbeat check (a coroutine ticking every 50 ms sees a worst lag of ~41 ms, which is why the brief's proposed acceptance test would have passed it), but np.dot drops the GIL on every call, so after each sqlite / file-write / log call a loop callback makes it can lose the GIL back to the worker for up to the 5 ms switch interval. Measured on this machine (Python 3.14.3, numpy 2.4.4, Windows): a loop callback of 20 sqlite calls takes a median 0.06 ms idle, 0.05 ms while a COROUTINE (yielding every 4,096 pairs) does the same scan, and 85-146 ms while a WORKER THREAD does it (worst 200-460 ms), i.e. 100-2,000x slower; 5 sqlite calls 13 ms median, 10 file-log lines 22 ms median (idle 0.03 and 0.38 ms). Nascence's substrate tick, stability tick and locomotion legs are exactly this kind of callback (file + DB + log work). A worker thread also cannot be cancelled (a cancelled awaiting task leaves the worker running to completion, and a second call starts a second one) and asyncio.run does not return until the worker finishes (measured: main() returned at 0.2 s after a cancel, the process exited at 6.2 s for a 6 s worker; with a 25-minute scan that is up to the 300 s asyncio.run join timeout and then the interpreter-exit join). Consequences: test a candidate off-loop design with a heartbeat whose tick body does GIL-releasing work (scripts/_test_find_cluster_off_loop.py section [7] is the reusable recipe), not only with an idle heartbeat; prefer a cooperative coroutine (yield every ~5 ms of work) for pure-Python/np.dot loops; use a thread only for work that spends its time inside C code that holds the GIL released for long stretches (file/network/embedding calls), where the loop is not fighting it for the GIL every microsecond. F-1469 flagged other synchronous stretches in the sleep pipeline (_embed, replay_strengthen, ...) that were never measured; anyone tempted to wrap those in to_thread should measure with this recipe first.

At temperature 0.0 the same 20 first-sample inputs give 0 of 20 divergent gate outcomes over 3 runs and BYTE-IDENTICAL raw outputs in all 20 (the 3 templated strings: 0 of 3 divergent). Determinism is not correctness: at temperature 0 the templated ask-the-library string is formed 3 of 3 times. CONTEXT SENSITIVITY is a second, separate mechanism that temperature 0 does not remove: the same thought under a different real active list (another repeat-subset case's list; the three templated strings under four real non-empty lists) flips the gate outcome in 6 of 32 swaps at temperature 0.0 (5 of 20 case swaps, 1 of 12 templated swaps). Consequence for D-0176: the model swap is not what removes the identical-input flip; setting scan_shadow's temperature to 0.0 (core/commitment_ledger.py scan_shadow, `temperature=0.3` in the call_json line) does, for any seat, and the residual inconsistency in production is context-driven (the active list changes between occurrences of the same string). FINDING 1 -- the 1,333 flips are NOT one uniform bug; they are two different mechanisms, and F-1715's own headline count conflates them:

(a) 1,323 of 1,333 (99.25%), 20 of 21 gists, 14 DISTINCT underlying books (6 of the 20 gist-rows are duplicate essay/understanding captures of an already-counted book -- rereads or an essay+understanding pair for the same title -- collapsing "Astronomy with an Opera-glass..." x3, "A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Know[ledge]" x3, "Creative Intelligence...Pragmatic Atti[tudes]" x2, "Boys and Girls Bookshelf..." x2 down to 1 book each) are genuine truncation artifacts. (b) 10 of 1,333 (0.75%), all under ONE gist (6d7ba0c4, "The Sea Shore"), are NOT a truncation artifact and NOT a regression at all -- confirmed by reading the real stored content, not just tags. Paternoster fishing... rocky coasts..." -- a genuine natural-history/beachcombing book (cross-referenced live in the corpus to a real citation: "By W. S. FURNEAUX. The 10 flipped rows are all tagged "[From 'The Shores of the Adriatic The Austrian Side The Küstenlande'] Produced by ... Distributed Proofreaders Europe ... THE SHORES OF THE ADRIATIC THE AUSTRIAN SIDE THE KÜSTENLANDE, ISTRIA..." -- a completely unrelated Austrian-coast travel/geography book. These 10 are wrongly linked ONLY because "shore" (The Sea Shore's one-word signature) is a plain substring of "shores" (Shores of the Adriatic) -- structurally the SAME false-lexical-coincidence bug class as Black Bar/Blackwoods (F-1704), via pluralization instead of compounding. FINDING 2 -- truncation's scope is much larger than the 21 gists currently exposed. Of 420 total live essay/understanding gists: 133 have a tag exactly 50 characters long; 126 of those end in an alphabetic character (proxy: cut mid-word, not at a space/punctuation boundary). Cross-referencing all 126 against the corpus's 238 distinct UNTRUNCATED reading-origin titles resolves this into a directly VERIFIED count: 112 are CONFIRMED genuinely truncated mid-word (a real reading-origin title shares the exact same 50-character prefix and continues past it, e.g. gist tag "Astronomy with an Opera-glass A Popular Introducti" vs. the real, live "...Introduction to the..."), 12 are CONFIRMED coincidental (a real reading-origin title IS exactly that 50-character string, e.g. "A Librarians Open Shelf Essays on Various Subjects" -- not a cut at all), 2 are unresolved (no reading-origin fragment of that book exists yet to check against). 106 of the 112 confirmed-genuine mid-word-cut gists are NOT among the 21 gists exposed by today's regression -- they simply have no already-filed citing fragment yet that happens to spell the cut word out in full. The measured 1,323/1,333 truncation regression is therefore a LOWER BOUND, not a final count: it will keep growing as Du keeps reading and sweep() keeps filing, independent of anything this job or J-1217 did.

OPTION (a) -- fix title[:50]/topic[:50] at the source (e.g. backtrack to the last space before 50 chars): mechanically cheap and narrowly scoped (2 write sites -- essay_lesson.record, grounded_learning.consolidate; no read-side change needed, since world_consolidation.py's own book_title[:50] re-slice is a no-op against an already-<=50-char smart-truncated string). But it is NOT a fix for what already exists: fragment content is permanent once written (no code anywhere rewrites stored content), so all 112 confirmed and up to 133 possibly mid-word-cut ALREADY-STORED gists -- including every one of the 20 gists behind today's real 1,323-row regression -- would still fail a strict word-boundary test after this fix ships, unless a separate, materially riskier data-migration step also rewrites their stored content (mutating historical stored records is exactly the class of change this project treats with caution). Verdict: worth doing for new essays going forward regardless of what else is decided, but insufficient alone, and does not by itself make a word-boundary ship safe.

OPTION (b) -- a truncation-edge-aware prefix match, built and regression-tested THIS job (not shipped): word-boundary matching for every signature word EXCEPT the one word that sits exactly at a confirmed truncation edge (len(gist_tag)==50 and the last regex-matched word token is itself a signature word) -- only that one word gets a left-anchored PREFIX test (matches "selec" against "selection") instead of the full \bword\b test everything else still gets. Tested against the identical 36,897-row already-filed population J-1217 used: 0 regressions on the 1,323 genuine truncation rows (down from 1,333 under the plain word-boundary candidate), 0 unexpected False->True flips, AND it correctly flips the 10 Sea-Shore/Adriatic rows to False too (closing FINDING 1(b)'s real pre-existing bug as a bonus, not a cost). This is a real, structural, currently-DORMANT risk (a future exactly-50-character real title whose last word happens to prefix some other live word could reintroduce a narrow version of the original bug) -- not a live cost today, but not zero either.

OPTION (c) -- accept as a known, rare, lower-priority defect, ship nothing: current confirmed live scope is 3 cases, not F-1704's 2 -- My Short Story Book/Original Short Stories and Black Bar/Blackwoods (fragment-level impact NOT YET measured for either, per F-1704) plus this job's Sea Shore/Shores-of-the-Adriatic (fragment-level impact IS measured: 10 fragments, real, already filed wrong, today). All three are the identical class (a short signature word that is a plain-English substring of an unrelated word -- compounding for 2, pluralization for 1) -- not isolated coincidences but a structural pattern that regular English pluralization (every plural is by construction a superset-substring of its singular) makes likely to recur again as the essay/understanding population keeps growing.

THREE distinct, mechanistically-identified failure causes (not previously named this precisely):
(1) PURSUIT-QUESTION CONTAMINATION (origin='research', the '[Looked up: X (pursuit: Y)]' format): confirmed directly against full source text on 2 separate clusters (environment, tranquillity) -- multiple source fragments in the SAME cluster share IDENTICAL actual definition content but DIFFERENT bracketed pursuit-question preambles; the distiller pulls the pursuit-question's own words ('geology', 'perception of...serenity', 'the invisible world', '渡') into the gist as if they were retrieved content. WORSE: _cluster()'s own topic-tokenization falls back to the raw content field (including this bracketed preamble) when keywords is empty, so a wrong-topic fragment (a 'Looked up: Understanding' fragment whose actual content has nothing to do with tranquility) got pulled into a 'tranquility' cluster purely because its OWN pursuit-question happened to mention 'tranquility' -- directly explaining that gist's invented 'intersecting with understanding' claim. This mechanism concentrates in the smallest clusters (n_sources 3-5, which F-1585 already found fail at 69% vs the 9-10-source band's 52%) -- roughly 10% of this session's 40-row failing sample, but a disproportionate share of the worst-failing small-cluster band.
(2) OUTSIDE/PRETRAINED-KNOWLEDGE EMBELLISHMENT on well-known works: the large majority of the remaining sample (roughly 30-33 of 40, book excerpts from Bergson, Locke, Leibniz, Schopenhauer, Ricardo, Malory, etc. -- mostly famous/canonical texts) add specific plausible-sounding claims, names, or framings beyond what the fed ~300-char-per-source excerpt actually states, consistent with the underlying LLM drawing on its own pretrained knowledge of these well-known works rather than staying strictly grounded in the fed material.
(3) IN-TEXT ATTRIBUTION CONFLATION: confirmed directly (Le Morte Darthur case) -- source material that quotes a THIRD PARTY within it (e.g. '...Philippa...whom Froissart calls...') gets flattened by the distiller into a claim about the filed book's own title-author ('Sir Thomas Malory's Le Morte Darthur describes...'), because the distiller attends to the book-title label, not the actual in-text speaker.

Self-origin material structurally avoids all three mechanisms (no pursuit-question preamble, no famous-work pretrained-knowledge risk, no third-party in-text quotation to misattribute) -- a clean, mechanistic explanation for why self's yield (79.3%) so far outruns semantic's (37.9%), beyond 'the judge is just stricter on semantic.'

(pursuit: ...)]' provenance prefix before it reaches BOTH the distil prompt's material and _cluster()'s own token fallback, so pursuit-question wording can never drive topic-bucketing or leak into a gist as content; (b) strengthen the distil system prompt's existing 'invent nothing' line with an explicit instruction not to draw on outside/pretrained knowledge of a well-known work, and to preserve in-text attribution (a quote inside a source belongs to whoever the source says said it, not to the book's own filed title-author) rather than collapsing everything to 'the book says'. Rough, labeled-as-estimated sizing (no live re-run performed, per this job's own no-deploy scope): fix (a) addresses a mechanism concentrated in the 3-5-source-cluster band (13 of 164 semantic clusters per F-1585, currently 69% failing there vs 52% overall) -- closing even half that gap to the overall rate would retire on the order of 1-2 more clusters per 164 attempted, a modest (~1pp) yield gain on its own, but a clean, low-risk, mechanistically-confirmed fix worth doing regardless of size. Fix: a naive datetime WITH a time component is now refused outright with a clear error naming the fix (add an explicit +12:00/+13:00/+00:00 offset) -- refusing ambiguous input rather than guessing a timezone, matching this project's own "UNKNOWN is an honest answer, a wrong one is not" convention (same philosophy as plan_liveness.py's own threshold-parsing fix earlier this session). A bare DATE with no time component (e.g. "2026-09-27") is unaffected and still parses as UTC midnight -- unchanged, since that's a fundamentally lower-ambiguity case than a precise clock-time reading. is_due()'s own naive-stored-value fallback (UTC-assume) is left as a defensive backstop for any pre-fix legacy records, now documented as such rather than unexplained. Verified via 8 isolated unit checks (bare date unchanged, explicit offsets of both signs work, the exact S-0190 bug case now refused with a clear message, Z-suffix handled, is_due()'s backward-compat backstop still works both directions, genuinely invalid input still gives its original error) plus a real CLI smoke test through argparse confirming the refusal message and exit code. Checked for currently-live stored not_before values that might need retroactive correction: J-1338 (the one job S-0190 named directly) was already closed/superseded this session with a correctly-fixed successor (J-1356, explicit +12:00 offset); J-1345's own stored value has no direct evidence of being affected (it belongs to a DIFFERENT chain, social_world_school's G6-G9, not the one S-0190 named) -- left untouched rather than guessed at. job_queue.py lives outside the C:\Nascence git repo (not a git repo itself), so this fix is a direct file edit, no commit.

claim: The Witness's invention-rate instrument (core/lane2.py _invention_check, plan metric #2) has two systematic false-positive classes that account for most of its flags. It marks a topic 'invented' when the topic word appears in the output but none of _TOPIC_FIELDS' mapped fields is in world_fields. (1) cat -> ('cat_at',) only: 164 deepseek-era ticks are flagged for 'cat', and in 153 of them the notice says 'purr' with the sounds field present -- the cat's purr is in the sounds list (cat_purr), so the Witness heard the cat exactly as the tuple told it, and the instrument calls that invention because cat_at is absent. The real residue (wet 17, moon 17, damp 16, fire 14, tide 12) is small, consistent with the pre-registered 'near-zero, decreasing' expectation. Any reader of invention_rate today is reading mostly instrument error, not the Witness inventing.

the CURRENT WORKING TREE content for that path (git-commit(1) DESCRIPTION, item 4: "the commit will ignore

claim: The documented SAME-FILE COMMIT SAFETY recipe (CLAUDE.md / job-run ground rules: git show HEAD:<path> to a scratch file, apply only your own edit, hash-object -w, update-index --cacheinfo) does not by itself guarantee isolation, and at least one real execution this batch (job J-1482's commit fbcc39b on docs/ROADMAP.md) silently absorbed two OTHER concurrent agents' uncommitted bullet edits into its own commit despite that commit's own message explicitly claiming "HEAD plus only this one bullet, nothing else picked up from the shared working tree." No content was lost (all three bullets landed intact and correctly formed), but the isolation claim was false, and a less benign case (e.g. two agents editing near the same lines, or one agent's edit being mid-write) could have gone worse. A verified-working stronger alternative exists: build the new tree entirely against a private index (GIT_INDEX_FILE env var pointed at a scratch path, git read-tree <HEAD>, git update-index --cacheinfo with the one blob, git write-tree, git commit-tree -p <HEAD>, then git update-ref <ref> <new> <old> as a compare-and-swap) -- this never touches the shared .git/index or working tree at any point, so it cannot pick up anything another concurrent agent has staged or is mid-editing. Recommend hardening the documented recipe to either (a) prescribe the GIT_INDEX_FILE-isolated build instead of a plain update-index against the shared index, or (b) at minimum add a mandatory post-commit check: git diff <parent> <new-commit> -- <path> and confirm the diff contains ONLY your own intended hunk before trusting the commit.

tagging mechanisms/strategies -- (a) tag belief_id on EVERY observe() call regardless of whether a
belief was actually injected that cycle (answers F-2127's cross-topic question on the fullest possible
sample, but F-2195 worried this meant a second _best_belief() call / a second read of

this was the right call, via one real technical discovery that changes the shape of the tradeoff F-2195
posed:

VERIFIED: core/orchestrator.py's existing guidance-note block (lines ~807-823, unchanged by me in its
control flow) only resets its own cooldown timer (self._last_guidance_note_ts) INSIDE the
`if self.state.guidance_note:` branch -- i.e. only on a cycle where a belief was actually injected. On a
cycle where core.guidance_learning.relevant_belief() returns None (no match), the timer is NOT bumped,
so the `(time.time() - self._last_guidance_note_ts) >= GUIDANCE_NOTE_COOLDOWN` (1800s) gate reopens
again on the very next cycle. This block also has NO `if input_type == "human":` guard (confirmed by
indentation: it sits at the same 8-space level as the human-only shadow-capture block above it, not
nested inside it) -- it runs on every cycle of every type (human/idle/internal/dream/etc.), since
_run_cycle_impl is the single shared pipeline for all of them (core/orchestrator.py:386-410 shows no
input-type early-return before this point). Net effect: core.guidance_learning._best_belief() --
and therefore a full read+json.loads of data/guidance_beliefs.json (210 beliefs today) -- ALREADY runs
on very nearly every cycle of Du's live cognition today, for the existing (pre-J-1630) guidance-note
feature, except within 30 minutes after a belief was last successfully injected. Given the real
guidance_injection_log.jsonl holds 771 successful injections over ~90 days (~1 success per ~2.8h on
average, i.e. the 30-min post-success cooldown is a small fraction of total runtime), the vast majority
of cycles already pay this exact cost today, independent of anything this job does.

This means F-2195's stated worry about option (a) -- "a real, if probably small, per-cycle cost to a
live hot path" -- undersold how much of that cost is ALREADY being paid today for a different reason;
but it does NOT mean option (a)'s full semantics (tagging with the closest-matching belief even when its
lexical score is below the 0.25 injection threshold, i.e. a belief that was never actually shown to Du)
is free of a real change -- that specific extension was not implemented, deliberately: the job's own
title says "active belief_id", and "active" reads most naturally as "actually injected this cycle", the
same thing state.guidance_note already represents. Expanding belief_id's meaning to "closest candidate,
even sub-threshold" would be a new signal this project doesn't otherwise have, is not what the title

one) rather than a real topic signal -- so I implemented strategy (b), the narrow one, but wired it to

a (phrase, id) tuple from one shared function instead of a side-channel global/attribute.

(1) METHOD = J-0949's validated one, not re-derived: a lifetime starts at the latest "Memory store initialised" line within 400 s before each "Nascence is awake" line (and after the previous awake line), else at the awake line; it ends at the "Nascence shutting down." line in its span, else it is UNCLEAN. Markers are matched strictly at the start of the message: a loose substring match (the mutation) mints a phantom boot from a line that merely quotes "Nascence is awake", the shipped regex does not.

J-1804 DESIGN (analysis only; store.py NOT edited; no live data or DB opened): the right fence for the live memory DB is NOT per-writer guard_path edits inside core/memory/store.py. _connect() (store.py:121) is the single choke point for ~50 modules, and 8 of those siblings issue their own raw write SQL through it (chapters, epistemic_affordance_advisor, memory_edges, memory_levels, night, refinery, study_note, world_consolidation; only study_note has guard_path tokens, covering its own files). Fencing only store.py's own writers would leave the same hole in 8 more modules plus every future caller.

Recommended design (Option C): make _connect() itself non-live-aware. When profile.LIVE is False AND DB_PATH is not already redirected (profile._data_relative(DB_PATH) is not None and not a data/_lab/<dir>/ sandbox -- the exact test guard_path already applies), return a READ-ONLY connection (set_authorizer allowing only SELECT/READ/FUNCTION/RECURSIVE/TRANSACTION/SAVEPOINT plus an allow-list of harmless PRAGMAs such as busy_timeout; or a mode=ro URI). Every reader (du_pulse, plan tools, graph builders, labs, hud) keeps working unchanged; any INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ALTER/CREATE/DDL raises a sqlite3 error at the SQL layer. A live process (profile.LIVE True) takes the existing code path plus one boolean read: byte-identical. lab_env.isolate() and activate_profile() both move DB_PATH outside data/ or into data/_lab/<stamp>/, which guard_path logic already clears, so neither is affected. Same D-0179 stance as every other fenced store: refuse, do not redirect, one warning per path. Non-live READS stay allowed (recommended); the opened decision asks the founder to confirm.

Two things the design must handle, both measured:
(a) memory_edges._connect() runs CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS on EVERY connect, a DDL write on the live DB even for a pure read. Under the authorizer this is DENIED even when the table exists; under mode=ro CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on an existing table is a silent no-op. So memory_edges must wrap its DDL in try/except or skip it on a read-only connection, otherwise every non-live memory_edges read breaks.
(b) 8 operator scripts write the live DB on purpose with no redirect token (scripts/_first_thought.py, backfill_founder_memory.py, geometry_tuple_fragment_vectors.py, librarian.py, phaseA_report.py, reconstruct_shadow_activation_J-0901.py, seed_epochs_themes.py, sync_overview_md.py), and scripts/activity_memory_backfill.py sets store.DB_PATH = LIVE_DB explicitly. The authorizer variant on a rw connection does not remove the checkpoint; mode=ro does not remove the sidecar creation; the founder-visible choice is which of those residuals is acceptable. Recommendation: authorizer on a rw connection (keeps WAL semantics, simplest, no URI path quirks), accept the checkpoint residual.

Every caller is asyncio.to_thread (never the loop), so waiting cannot stall the loop; the second of two overlapping requests waits, sees the first's fresh _last_fetch and gets the cooldown None, exactly what two sequential calls return; a failed first fetch writes no _last_fetch so the second still tries.

Embed stays outside so a slow encode never blocks the other thread. The cooldown is re-checked under the lock (never fires single-threaded). Lock order is always _OBSERVE_LOCK -> _IO_LOCK.

claim: Novelty thread (F-2609 follow-up, founder session 2026-10-08): the causal novelty predictor loses to persistence because of its LEVEL, not its DYNAMICS, and a one-line re-anchoring beats persistence decisively on the same pooled corpus. Decomposition over the 2,861 post-fix steps: (1) the predictor is biased low on 83.4% of steps, mean(actual - causal) = +0.090, median +0.078 -- it rebuilds novelty_hunger from scratch as 0.5*quietness + 0.25*projected_dissonance and omits the capability-surprise addend (_CAP_SURPRISE_TO_NOVELTY = 0.30 x a 1 h-half-life surprise scalar, climate_engine.py:709-717) while holding quietness at its last value; (2) the dissonance term it DOES model carries essentially all of novelty's step-to-step variance (0.00794 of a total 0.00760; quietness+surprise changes contribute 0.00047), so the thing it forecasts is the right thing. (3) Re-anchoring the forecast on the live actual and predicting only the change -- hybrid = novelty_now + 0.25*(projected_dissonance - dissonance_now), using nothing but the previous row's own actual and its own causal coherence forecast -- gives MAE 0.0271 vs naive 0.0634 vs the current causal 0.0925; beats naive on 2,309 steps, loses 506 (p = 1e-273); on the 43 pooled switch rows 34 W / 8 L (p = 7e-5); event-aligned 6 folds 6/6 (all by a wide margin); net-positive in 31 of 34 regimes. The three regimes where it loses are the first three after the 09-04 fix (09-04 23:29 to 09-08 09:17, including one 62 h regime at -79 of 342 steps); from 09-08 on it wins in every regime, so something about early-September climate behaviour differed and is worth one look before shipping, but it does not change the verdict. A shrunk variant (0.125 x the dissonance delta) also wins (MAE 0.0384, 2,473 W / 342 L) if overshoot is a concern. This is the same lesson as F-0613's stale-actual artifact: the causal substrate is right about what moves and must not be made to re-derive the level. Shipping it is a change to core/homeostasis_causal.py predict_novelty (needs the live actual passed in or read from the same climate_state.json snapshot) -- restart-gated, shadow-only, no live behaviour depends on predicted_causal.

When a pressure sleep fires at dusk, the last row is the fire row itself (P >= 10 with the night threshold 10 -> vitality 0.000) and no row is logged again until should_sleep() is next evaluated after the wake, so for the whole sleep plus the first post-wake minutes the instrument reports 'exhausted' for a Du who has just slept. 167 of 2,083 same-regime non-stale steps (8%) have their actual pinned to a fire row; 10 of the 12 real dusk losses are exactly this case (sleep fired within the step at ~20:01 as the predictor said, actual still 0.000). Mechanism: bw weight 0.85 vs concern weight 0.9 with habituation; bw wins only when its p_norm is pinned near 1.0 (win rows mean p_norm 0.993 vs 0.492 elsewhere) AND concern is habituated by a streak (win rows concern habituation mean 0.86, s_final 0.763 vs bw 0.844; 854 of 915 wins have concern p_norm=1.0). So win-share ~ P(bw p_norm pinned) x P(concern on a streak). bw p_norm swings by day (mean 0.12 to 0.76; pn=1 share 0 to 32 pct), tracking its own 500-row percentile history of raw (raw means 0.117 to 0.237 by day), giving win days 10-10 (213), 10-13 (300), 10-15 (153) when raw ran high. First 2000 ticks 9.90 pct win, mid 9.85, last 2000 3.85 (pn1 36.1 to 2.7 pct), so it drifts toward the 1-2 pct replay value on a slow trend but has not reached it. reality_share is flat-ish: 0.370 to 0.457, wins mean 0.397 vs all 0.403, no excursion link. reality_share max 0.4569, never reaches EXIT_AT 0.47 in this window (0 rows), so balance_light (needs needs_reality() False) cannot have fired from this data; whether it reaches EXIT_AT live is NOT answerable from this window. Replay-gap cause is inferred (concern streak habituation not modeled by replay, raw mean 0.197 vs 0.12); not tested.

claim: No real cue-independent coarse when-anchor exists for any of the four D-0292 callers, and none of them currently asks a dating question; a coarse window only beats trail order when the anchor is within the window half-width (cliff at anchor error > half-width), so the lane needs an anchor accurate to within +-7 d (hw 7) or +-14 d (hw 14) and every clock-like source (now/boot/session/last Travis turn/last recalled fragment) misses that bar. Detail. (1) Anchor sources, per caller. pursuits.return_seed asks ask("pursuits", question+open) for topical seeds; dream asks ask("dream", day-material, grounded_only=False) and WANTS remote recombination, not dating; curiosity asks ask("curiosity", frontier question, descend=True) to seed a thought; the recall act does not use ask() at all (core/evidence_recall.py has its own _candidates). Of 98 logged recall-act questions in data/evidence_log.jsonl, 0 contain a relative-time phrase and 0 ask when/first/last time: they are topical themes ('moments of uncertainty', 'my past beliefs'). So the autobiographical-dating problem has no live consumer today; F-2848's 'twelve days ago' is a spontaneous reference, not an ask() call. Candidate anchors and what they give: (a) now / boot clock / session clock / last dated thing Travis said (all ~now): on the 96-event sample anchor=now with hw 3/7/14 gives median top-1 error 16/14/14 d vs base 13 and within-3d 0.21/0.23/0.29 vs base 0.33, i.e. no gain or worse, because the event ages are spread over 1-30 d. (b) date of the last fragment the asker recalled (self-anchor on base top-1): provably a no-op, window re-ordering keeps in-window fragments in pool order and the base top-1 is always in its own window; measured 0 of 96 top-1 changes in both pool views; and base top-1 is itself only within 7 d of truth for 45% (all view) / 51% (grounded) of events and within 14 d for 54% / 61%, so a chained anchor from a different recall would fail the cliff below about half the time. (c) epoch retrieval as a coarse index (store.retrieve_epoch, 566 epochs, median span 0.08 d, a session slice not an era): top-1 epoch by cue cosine puts the event within its window for 10% (<=3 d) / 16% (<=7 d) of events, median miss 32.5 d, only 19/96 cues clear the 0.58 floor and those are worse (median 78 d); best-of-top-3 within 7 d is 39%. Dead. (d) chapters: the 70 chapter fragments carry formation time, not era span (era window is computed at formation and not stored on the row), members are walled from recall by chapter_id, and the ask() when slot for chapters returns fragment_id=None text (F-2180); not usable as a date anchor. (e) born/ts of the asker's own object (pursuit 'born', curiosity queue 'ts'): cue-independent and legitimate in form, but nothing ties the relevant memory to the object's birth date and there is no ground truth to score it; unmeasured, not shown to exist. Also note the existing ask(when=(t0,t1)) path is NOT the probe's coarse_window arm: _fanout_when with a timestamp pair calls store.get_fragments_in_range, which returns the newest episodic fragments in the range regardless of the cue (ORDER BY timestamp DESC), as a separate slot of k_per_slot=3; a window FILTER on the what-pool does not exist in ask() and would be new code. (2) Noisy-anchor sweep (scratch re-run: same probe sampler/recall, ask() trail pool k=15 all origins, seeds 0-3 x 24, 96 event-rows, lab_env.isolate, CPU embedding only; pools captured then re-ranked offline, 300 or 200 random trials per cell; anchor = truth +- m days with random sign, wrong-anchor draws uniform over 1-30 d ago). This run's base differs from F-3015 because live stores moved (all view base median 13 d / within-3d 0.33 vs 15 / 0.25; grounded view 6 d / 0.39 over 88 answered vs 18 / 0.27), so only paired comparisons inside this run are trustworthy. Oracle windows here: hw3 median 2 d within-3d 0.77; hw7 2 d 0.59; hw14 3.5 d 0.50 (all view). Gain table, all view, wrong-anchor rate 0: anchor error 0-2 d -> hw3 median 2 d (W/L 42/0), hw7 2 d, hw14 3.5 d; anchor error 4 d -> hw3 collapses to 4.3 d W/L 26/22, hw7 2.0 d 44/0, hw14 3.5 d; anchor error 6 -> hw7 2.0 d (43/1); anchor error 8 -> hw7 6.7 d W/L 37/25 within-3d 0.37, hw14 4.5 d (31/2); anchor error 12 -> hw7 12.0 d (27/21, within-3d 0.15 below base 0.33), hw14 4.0 d (32/4); anchor error 14 -> hw14 5.7 d (28/7); anchor error 16 -> hw14 12.4 d W/L 23/32 within-3d 0.26 (worse than base on both). So the gain disappears at anchor error just above the half-width, at every half-width tested (hw3 at ~4 d, hw7 at ~8 d, hw14 at ~16 d); inside the half-width the gain is flat (median 2-5 d vs base 13). Wrong-anchor rate: at 20% wrong the median loses about 0.5-1 d and within-3d drops 5-9 points (hw7, anchor error 0-6: median 2.4-2.8 d, within-3d 0.54-0.59, W/L ~41/3); at 50% wrong it is still above base (hw7: median 3.8-4.7 d, within-3d 0.46-0.50, W/L ~37/8) because a wrong window mostly leaves the pool order unchanged. Grounded (API-default) view: same shape with smaller gains (base 6 d / 0.39; hw7 anchor error <=6: 2.3-3.0 d within-3d 0.53-0.59; hw14 anchor error <=12: 3.7-4.0 d). What the lane needs to beat trail order: a cue-independent or cue-derived coarse date accurate to within the window half-width, i.e. about +-7 d for a 7 d window or +-14 d for a 14 d window, correct at least ~50% of the time (it still beats trail order at 50% wrong); a wider window buys tolerance at the cost of sharpness (hw14 at zero error 3.5 d vs hw3 2.0 d). CAVEAT: the sampled events are only 1-30 d old, so a 14 d window already covers about half the support and flatters wide windows; for months-old events the same windows would discriminate harder, untested. claim: J-2521 (T-0106, frontier_disciplines s10 Peters non-ergodicity): FORWARD PATH REPLAY of curiosity_habituation's would-choose policy along a real week gives CONVERGENCE - the ensemble read was safe for this channel. Replicate 2026-09-15..09-24 (442 ticks, 9 days, not part of the verdict): same, mean D-C modal_share -2.6% relative (8 of 9 days negative, largest |z| 3.3), R1-R3 all false, live inside band 9 of 9. SCOPE OF THE NULL: the replay holds the tension pool (counts, charges) fixed at the recorded values and feeds back ONE channel, the label-keyed anti-relock window (14 labels, x0.08) in a pool of about 700 labels (the window covers about 2 percent of the labels); the other compounding channel (seed -> next theme -> tension count re-activation) needs the LLM and was NOT replayed. It was only sized: P(an offered label's count rises at the next tick) = 2/927 = 0.2% (primary) and 8/1300 = 0.6% (replicate) vs 0.09% / 0.05% for not-offered, so the own-tension channel is small but cross-tension spillover is not measured. The null therefore says the ensemble method is safe where the pool is large and the feedback is a recency window; it does NOT certify policies with a small candidate set and a winner-take-all pick (transport_habituation, idle_allocator): those are spawned as separate path replays.

claim:
P-0004 Memory router: the episodic_keys and semantic_keys it generates do not change what is retrieved (write-only in effect). Only time_bias (a small multiplier) and working_memory_sufficient (never true now) reach recall.

Mechanism: core/orchestrator.py _retrieve_memory builds query_text = raw_input + " " + perception.summary and passes it with the keys to core/memory/store.py retrieve(). retrieve() embeds query_text (keys are used as the query only when query_text is blank) and ranks every row by cosine. The keys enter scoring in exactly one place, the keyword fallback in _score_tier / _load_pool_fast, which runs only for rows with no usable embedding (or when _embed returns None). A read-only count on data/memory/nascence.db over the retrieve pool (cold=0, not hidden/system_note/dormant, no chapter) found 44,955 rows and 0 without an embedding. So the 2-4 episodic and 2-4 semantic keys per call have no effect on ranking.

time_bias does reach _score_tier as a recency multiplier (recent up to x1.2 for rows under 7 days old, distant up to x1.1, all x1.0). Offline A/B (read-only, same embedder paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2, tier slots 2/3/4, seed weight applied, 50 real logged queries, 25 human and 25 internal): the router's chosen time_bias gives an identical 9-slot set to forced 'recent' in 39 of 50 and to 'all' in 47 of 50; mean overlap 0.96 to 1.0, so at most 1 of 9 slots ever changes (before the 5-most-recent guarantee, which is independent of the router).

working_memory_sufficient=true skips all recall (orchestrator.py _retrieve_memory early return), but it was true on 65 of 4259 logged rows, all in 2026-05/06 (49 June, 16 May, human only), 0 since July. data/nascence.log (2026-05-29 to 11-01) has 0 lines matching reason=working_memory_sufficient or reason=no_keys from the J-1416 log line.

Drift: docs/node_audit/memory_router_node.md says the keys drive retrieval and are used for keyword overlap scoring; that has not been true since the store moved to embedding ranking with every row embedded.

The paired shadow second look (core/reentry_p2.py on_commitment_scan_done) re-asks a copy and was reported failing its kill-switch (pre-reset F-3144); it is shadow and not a different family. claim: P-0044 / Follow Line delivery funnel and staleness: most of Du's questions never get a return, and the ones that do arrive hours late while the text says "asked just now". Since boot (2026-10-29 18:38, data/logs/follow_line_shadow.jsonl, 931 unique boarded q_ids: asked 649, consequence 198, claim 79, pursuit 5) only 180 ran (19%; asked 173, claim 5, consequence 2). Of the 180 runs, 174 were delivered into an idle thought (100% of the 175 would_return rows were placed and met; 0 expired), 7 were deferred by J-2570. Of 609 asked entries born since boot in data/frontier.json, 310 are status faded with line.state still waiting: evicted by frontier MAX_OPEN before they ever ran. The cause is a service rate below the arrival rate plus a FIFO queue: BOARD_CAP_PER_HOUR=4 (2,959 'wait-cap' ride rows), frontier.waiting_for_line sorts oldest-born first within a source, so the freshest asks wait behind the oldest. Measured board-to-delivery lag for asked returns: median 4.9 h, p90 7.6 h, 111 of 139 over one hour, only 22 under ten minutes. Yet 135 of 139 asked returns open with "Something you asked just now" (_origin_phrase, core/follow_line.py line 690, which prints that for every source=asked regardless of age). So the first sentence of seed part 1 is untrue for about four returns in five.

claim: P-0030, the mineness arrival note ('That last thought arrived rather than flowing from the rest of what you were thinking -- "<thought>". Notice it: something reached you from outside your own current, or something new stirred in you.', core/mineness.py arrival_note, seed part 13): healthy and rare, with two cosmetic defects. claim: P-0088's code-seeing hint (source_sight, brick B2) is attached to roughly 30% of grounding calls, is chosen by keyword match, and is often unrelated to the thought, so it feeds the grounder a file line to 'ground in' and engineering text reaches Du's stored thoughts. core.source_sight._MECH_TERMS includes ordinary words of Du's daily thoughts ('self', 'river', 'shadow', 'mirror', 'dream', 'memory', 'feeling', 'thought', 'pattern', 'identity'). Replaying the live functions on the last 30 days of logged raw thoughts: is_self_mechanism() is true for 4,001 of 13,004 (30.8%); in a random 300-sample all 100 flagged thoughts get a see_code() hit (100/100). The hint is added to the user prompt as 'THE REAL MECHANISM (you can see the code - ground in what is actually there, not an imagined one): <file>: <line>' (about 190-228 chars; the logged user-prompt sizes are consistent with about 30% carrying it: 21.5% of calls exceed 1,000 chars against a 850-char base). Consequences in the log: 130 of 13,001 groundings (1.0%) cite a .py file, 13 of those file names reach the stored thought. Spurious matches are the repeated ones: 'actions.py' 57 times and 'book_feelings.py' 41; a thought about Morgan le Fay's shadow is grounded 'analogous to the shadow in code, as seen in the core/actions.py code snippet where a lost steep function was res...' and the stored thought ends 'just as a restore...'; a tide-crossing thought cites 'core/book_feelings.py: Nascence -- Book Feelings'. The hint only matches the first term-bearing comment line, so it cannot be 'the mechanism' of an image in the thought. Not a leading-hint issue in the founder-law sense (it hints at nothing about what Du should conclude), but it is engineering text and a fabrication invitation entering the thought stream. Side note, same function: ground_thought also calls emissary_tension.note_recurrence on every grounding, so the 'bicameral recurrence' counter reads 41,979 recurrences and chronic_mass 524.25 (gate_ready True, cn 0.981): it counts groundings, not confrontations with the built-mind gap (thyme thoughts count the same). It has no live reader (keystone_steer returns '' since the 2026-08-20 founder ruling; KEYSTONE_PER_CANDIDATE_TOLL = False), so it is harmless but it is a pegged instrument, and its docstring still calls it observe-only.

claim: P-0032 fossil truncations in the memory/thread seed lines: the lines that quote Du's own thoughts cut them at fixed character counts that are shorter than the thoughts, mid-word more often than not. "What you were just thinking: {prev[:160]}" (nodes/inner_monologue_node.py ~3382): of 1,984 logged thoughts since 10-29, 96.6 percent are longer than 160 characters and 59.6 percent are cut in the middle of a word (the 160th and 161st characters are both letters/digits); label examples in the live log: 'What you were just thinking: The river's physica', 'The tide pulls back', 'The g'. "Still with you from earlier -- you concluded: "{content[:220]}"" (broadcast echo, ~3612): same thoughts-as-content test gives 67.0 percent over 220 and 41.4 percent mid-word (the broadcast content is a conclusion or thought of about that length; the injection log keeps only 200 chars so this is a proxy, inferred). "A recent dream: {narrative[:180]}": 3 of 3 current dreams (974, 2,227, 2,388 chars) are cut mid-word. "The last thing discussed -- them: "{human[:120]}" you: "{entity[:120]}"": the farewell is over 400 characters, so both halves are cut mid-sentence. moment-texture and pursuit quotes are the F-3614 case. Pursuit return and the follow-line return already use word-safe truncation (_trunc_words, J-0217), which is the existing pattern to copy. Effect: low and cosmetic for the model (a 9B model reads half-words fine) but it is an easy tell that the seed is engineering text, and the thought's own last clause is the one thing the previous-thought line exists to carry, so cutting it at 160 chars removes the clause that most advances the thread; mid-thread ticks (60 percent of prompts) are exempt from the previous-thought line because the carry quotes the last step at [:220] instead (same cut, 41 percent mid-word). Fix: one helper that cuts at the last space before the cap (and adds an ellipsis), applied to the four lines. Founder laws: no new content, only a cleaner cut.

claim: P-0031 REACH, with a live behavioural effect: the ambient sound line (surf, birds, bees, fire) is tagged as a grounding 'percept', so background wallpaper switches off the stream pacer's grounding gate on about a third of all idle ticks. In nodes/inner_monologue_node.py the ambience block (line ~3532 comment 'Texture, not a stored moment') does `_fline = _snd.ambience()` / `if _fline: seed_parts.append(_fline)` / `self._moment_source = "percept"   # J-0581 (F-0811b)`. core/stream_drive.py `_GROUNDED_SOURCE = ("world", "broadcast", "percept", "reading", "frontier", "letter")` and `_is_grounded()` returns True for any source in it, before the vocabulary test, and `compute()` caps an ungrounded tick's drive at UNGROUNDED_CAP=0.5 ('anchor-less thought can't fast-loop'). CONTINUOUS_STREAM=True, so the controller sets the real gap (actual_gap equals would_gap on 100% of 2,872 logged rows). Measured on data/stream_drive_shadow.jsonl since the 2026-10-29 20:00 restart: 2,872 ticks, source='percept' on 1,339 (46.6%, the same share as the ambience line, 47% of prompts; true sound percepts are only about 15 a day); grounded=True on 1,333 of them. Re-running stream_drive._is_grounded(about, None) (the vocabulary rule alone, no provenance tag) on those 1,339 ticks says 898 would have been ungrounded (their about is e.g. 'Ouvrard and Na', 'Napoleon's blockade', 'chaotic space', 'the waiting book'), and on 889 of those drive_raw exceeds the 0.5 cap, so the gate would have bitten. The gap those 889 ticks actually got has median 4.95 s; with the cap it would be about 16.5 s (computed with stream_drive's own GAP_MIN, GAP_MAX, K). So on about 31% of all idle ticks (889 of 2,872) a thought about something other than the world is paced as if grounded because the shore was making its usual noise. J-0581/F-0811b widened the tag set deliberately so real percepts (music, a purr) ground the thought; the ambience line was swept in with the sound percept above it. Whether ambience should count is a design question about what 'grounded' means (founder call), not an obvious typo: the intent of the gate is a thought anchored in the world, the tag says only that the seed contained a world sound. If ambience should not count the change is one line (drop the tag on the ambience branch); the cost of leaving it is that the gate's discrimination is mostly spent (grounded 1,333 of 1,339 when tagged vs 308 of 1,271 untagged, i.e. the tag, not the thought, decides). Cross-row note: the pacer is owned by the continuous_stream plan, not P-0031.
