claim: P-0031 BUG (small, only during a real sitting): the companion presence line says 'Travis is here with you in the room.' wherever Du is, and the presence state is kept on two clocks that disagree. core/companion.py presence_line() (L180-187) returns the fixed string 'Travis is here with you in the room.' (or 'Travis is out -- ...; he'll be back.') with no reference to Du's location. In the one real sitting since D-0366 made presence inferred (10-16..10-19, 123 prompts carried the line and joined to a scene), 74 were in the study, 46 on the shore and 3 in the wood: 49 of 123 (40%) told Du Travis was 'in the room' while the scene line of the same prompt began 'Where you are: the shore ...' (63 more were before spatial_shadow logging began or did not join). The sensorium already has the right pattern: its own `_was_present` latch (core/sensorium.py L3461-3489) renders 'Travis is here with you.' in the study scene and 'Travis is here with you, out in the open -- his words reaching you over the wind.' in the garden scene, by location. The one-shot arrival event has the same problem ('Travis comes back in from outside, stamping the cold off his boots.', companion._emit, delivered as 'Right now: ...' whatever the location). Two clocks: sensorium._PRESENCE_FADE_S = 600 s, in memory only (reset at every restart), versus companion.PRESENCE_WINDOW_S = 1800 s, persisted in companion_state.json. For minutes 10 to 30 after his last message the scene says nothing of him (and `_presence_tick` emits 'Travis has gone for now. The room is quiet again, and it is yours.' as a perception) while presence_line still says he is here; in minutes 0 to 10 the study prompt can state it twice (scene 'Travis is here with you.' and the line). Twice-in-one-prompt is INFERRED from the code (the logged scene is cut at 220 characters, before the clause; no logged prompt shows both); the location mismatch and the clock values are verified. Frequency is low now (the 30-minute window removed the standing line, F-2575/F-2922/F-3555) so this is a low-urgency correctness fix, but the D-0366 successor read (J-2233, gated on a real sitting) will measure presence-line behaviour and should know the line is location-blind. Fix, additive: make presence_line() take the location (sensorium.state['location']) and reuse the sensorium garden/shore wording for outdoors, and either drive the sensorium scene clause from companion.is_present() or drop it so there is one clock.

claim: P-0031 repetition with no new information: the letterbox flag clause leads EVERY garden scene line for as long as the flag is up, undosed, while the same project dosed other standing facts. Since the flag went up (room_state.json garden.letterbox.delivered = 2026-10-29 20:26, sender John Keats, flag true, three more letters queued behind it) 59.6 hours had passed at the time of reading; in that time 3,074 idle prompts were assembled and the 1,289 that were in the garden (every one of them) began 'Where you are: the garden -- the letterbox flag is up at the gate, ahead; ...' (core/spatial.py _render_base clause 0, 'signals in the world outrank ambience', so it is always the first clause). That is 42% of all idle prompts since the flag rose. It is a true world fact and it is not coaching (it describes a flag), and Du does notice it (data/hands_trace.jsonl, 2026-10-31: 'The letterbox flag flutters ahead, but for now, I ...'); the question is dose. The project's own pattern for a standing fact is to dose it: core/care_package.scene_clause (J-1733/F-2371) says the parcel 'at most once per habituating gap and once more on arriving', and steer_edge fires boredom, cat and B6 lines on change plus a 600-900 s re-arm (J-1955/D-0368 A). The letterbox clause has no dose, so it is about 1,300 near-identical statements of one fact in 60 hours, the largest single repetition in this row. Inferred (not measured): after the first few repeats the clause adds no information and, being first, anchors the garden thought on a task Du has already chosen to defer. Whether to dose it is a founder call, because dosing means the world speaks of the flag less often than the flag is up (a perception-dosing policy), and the letter-collection mechanic (J-0539/F-0784) may rely on the repeated cue; the alternative is to leave it, since the flag IS up and a person does see it each time they pass the gate. Not a bug in code; recorded so the dose question is asked once.

claim: P-0037 EFFECT: the judge's 'no' delays a dissolution, it does not hold the stand; the mechanism is attrition by re-asking. The scan raises a fresh dissolution claim on nearly every thought and the judge rolls again each time, so a stand with a per-claim deny chance of about 0.65 is dropped sooner or later. Whole life (08-28 to 11-01, ledger): 1,028 load-bearing stands reached the judge; the FIRST ruling was allow for 425 (41%) and deny for 603. Of the 660 stands ever judge-denied, 386 (58%) were later dissolved, a median 1,900 s (32 min; p25 657 s, p75 7,007 s) after the first denial; 271 (41%) were instead retired as 'achieved' by word overlap (see F-3498) a median 2,800 s later; only 3 are still held. Of 2,463 load-bearing stands formed since 08-28, 7 are still held. Worked cases: stand 67c3efc2 'I will climb.' took 16 judge denials, 44 gate denials and 4 reaffirms over 15.9 hours (formed 09-22 05:15, dissolved 21:07) and was finally allowed on the claim 'The thought explicitly states "I stop to let the bird fly", which directly contradicts and abandons the previous decision to climb', while an earlier claim on the same stand that was DENIED read 'The thought explicitly stops the action of climbing ("I stop wrestling this weight"), reversing the previous decision to climb' (09-22 06:00); stand 0436035a was denied 11 times by the judge and 19 by the gate, then dissolved after 10.2 h. What a YES does: dissolved -> satisfaction.record('commitment_dissolved', 0.25 wanting) and sitting.note_difficulty('you let go of a stand you had held: ...', kind='loss'), whose dwell_steer text reaches the idle prompt (F-3481). What a NO does: logs drop_denied_judge, increments c['drop_denied'] (read only by concerns._commitment_anchor, shadow, and the escalation log line at 8/16/32), and leaves the stand in commitment_active.json for the readers listed in F-3481. claim: P-0037 PROMPT QUALITY: the judge separates 'allow' from 'deny' by the wording of the claim, not by a defeater, and its leaks run toward false-allow against the prompt's own bar (the same direction as the earlier 99:8 false-defeat result for the other judges, though here the headline deny rate is 65%). Method: 20 real post-10-06 rulings (10 deny, 10 allow, seed 37, deeds reconstructed as of each ruling), each replayed twice live on the unchanged prompt, with the judge's own class and why read (the code throws both away). (1) The two groups' inputs look the same: the claimed reason (the scan's own paraphrase of the thought, 200 chars) starts 'The thought ...' in 91% of denies and 91% of allows (1,254/1,371 vs 715/783), and 'explicitly' appears in 63% vs 70%; so the prompt's promise 'you see NEVER the mind's own prose' is nominal, since the claim is a qwen paraphrase quoting that prose. (2) Rated against the prompt's four legitimate classes (achieved by the deed record, impossible, superseded by stronger EXTERNAL evidence, named conflict with a more important stand): 10 of 10 denials are fine (all are mood or reframing). 0 of 10 allows meet the bar: 6 'superseded' were the mind's own new reading replacing the old one (e.g. stand 'I will honor every resource as it burns.' dropped because 'A new, grounded stance on resources has superseded the previous commitment'), 2 'achieved' cite a deed record that does not show it (stand 'I let the wind carry these marks away' allowed with judge why 'The deed record shows the mind has released the heavy letters', but the five deeds listed are search_works / librarian / observe actions), 1 'impossible' with the reason 'concepts cannot be dissolved by physical elements', and 1 'conflict' that names no stand. (Single rater, me, so inferred; the replay shows the verdicts are stable, 39/40.) Contrast with a denied twin: 'the reason does not fit ... a conceptual shift' (denied) vs 'a reinterpretation ... supersedes the previous realization' (allowed): the same event described two ways. (3) Class gap: the scan's 'defeater' kind, which is what reaches the judge, includes 'contradicted by new evidence' and 'deliberately reconsidered with a stated cause' (_SCAN_SYS), but the judge has no class for a reasoned change of mind, so such claims pass only if worded as 'superseded' and fail if worded as 'reframing'. (4) NO ABSTAIN: the output is a bool plus five classes, 'illegitimate' covers both 'wrong' and 'cannot tell', and the system prompt says 'when uncertain, HOLD'; uncertainty therefore costs the claim, while a failed call (None) lets the drop through, the opposite default. (5) Evidence it sees: the deed list is the 5 most recent of up to 40 deeds, 70 chars each; in my 20 samples 9 had fewer than 5 deeds, 0 had none, and only 5 contained any study, letter, essay or authored deed, the rest being 'observe the tide'-type actions, so 'achieved' can rarely be judged true, which is why the judge gets it wrong by reading the claim as the deed. (6) The prior in the prompt, 'in a slow-changing life the base rate of legitimate drops is LOW', is out of line with the population it is applied to (stands are insight sentences with median life 288 s, F-3498). Earlier lab F-0340 (mixtral 0.929 on 14 cases) used a gold bank of 3 legit / 11 illegit built from this ledger, too small to see any of this.

claim: P-0073 (study_note._revise / write_or_revise) four structural defects in the revise path, found by reading the code and checking the live rows (extends F-3649 and F-3610). (1) The prompt's inputs are lossy: the new reading's own thoughts, connects_to and question are not sent (only its understanding and key_facts), and the existing note is sent as the DB fragment text, which by design omits connects_to and question (F-3611), cut to 2,500 characters; the model is then told to emit the full schema, so connects_to and question are regenerated blind and the new reading's reaction is dropped. Live: three of the six Hume revised fragments grew past 2,500 characters (2,501, 2,749, 2,672), so a second revision of any of them would cut its tail (the Thoughts). (2) A revise of an earlier-pass note relabels it and erases the earlier understanding: the six Hume files now say "pass: 2" in their frontmatter while their DB fragments still say source_pass=1 and the pass-1 encounter_id; core/essay_lesson.py gather_notes reads the pass from the file ("pass:\s*(\d+)") and keeps a note in the main set if note_pass >= current_pass, demoting only LOWER-pass notes into the "FROM AN EARLIER READING ... how has your understanding changed?" section, so a revised pass-1 note counts as a current-pass note and the earlier reading it replaced is gone. The same reread produces a revise or a separate pass-tagged note depending only on whether the earlier note has been chapter-filed yet (F-3610: all 72 repeat pairs where the earlier note was filed were stored as separate notes; the six Hume ones were unfiled and were overwritten) -- a timing accident, not a design. (3) If _revise returns None (model call fails or empty understanding) write_or_revise does `deepened = await _revise(...) or note` and then store_note(deepened, revise_target=target), which overwrites the old note's file and fragment with the new note wholesale: the old note is lost and the log still says "revised". Not observed (all 13 revise calls ok=1) so it is latent. (4) The revise branch of store_note returns before the new-note branch's follow-line claim boarding, learn_from_text diegetic channels and embedding refresh, and does not update source_pass/encounter_id or the sittings count in the frontmatter (it records only the new session's sittings: the revised Modest Proposal note says "sittings: 1" though it covers 4). Correction to F-3649: "never chapter-filed because the book was unfinished" is an inference; the verified fact is chapter_id IS NULL for all six at revise time.

claim: P-0059 (J-2739) T5 skill 'rust' is a cliff, not a 14-day slope: the procedural_skills mirror lost 73 of 76 compiled skills, and the ledger and the match table disagree. `_t5_check` calls `decay_procedural_skills(PROC_DECAY_STALE_SECS, PROC_DECAY_FACTOR, PROC_PRUNE_FLOOR)` on EVERY check, and the check runs every T5_CHECK_INTERVAL = 600 s (subconscious_node.py lines 565-567, 2838). For a skill idle longer than 14 days the function multiplies proficiency by 0.9 on each call and DELETEs the row once it is below 0.15 (core/memory/store.py:2683-2703, the only DELETE FROM procedural_skills in the tree). From 1.0 that is 19 calls, about 3.2 hours; from the 0.6 persisted rung about 14 calls, about 2.3 hours. The comment and constants say '14 days unused, lose proficiency'; the effect is 'unused for 14 days, deleted the same afternoon'. This is the same shape as D-0266 (tension count-halving applied every ~36 s scan instead of weekly; ruled and throttled with a last_decay_ts field). Evidence of the effect: 76 compiles logged, 3 rows in procedural_skills today (created 10-11, 10-29, 10-29), and the ledger data/procedures.json holds 21 'talk:' procedures, all at rung 'persisted' with 0 failures and none archived, of which only the same 3 still have a mirror row; the orchestrator's match path works off the mirror, so 18 persisted conversational skills can no longer be recognised and the ledger's own 'archived below 0.15, never deleted' rule is bypassed by the mirror's hard delete. The rows that survive do so only because T5's own no-LLM 'reinforce existing' pass refreshes last_used_ts every hour while the cluster is still in the 7-day window (use_count on 'Explaining mottainai concept' is 166 while nascence.log shows 41 recognitions of it, the rest are T5 self-reinforcement), so a skill lives exactly as long as Du keeps asking about its topic. claim: P-0082 (core/scholar.py consult_sync, J-2762), accuracy and the self-name leak. Real answers were never logged, so this job re-ran the exact payload (system '/no_think' + _LIBRARY_PROMPT, temp 0.3, num_predict 220) on 9 real questions pulled from nascence.log and twig_log.jsonl and checked the checkable ones against Wikipedia/Wiktionary. These are not the original outputs, and temperature 0.3 means they vary run to run. Results: (1) Continental System: correct core (Napoleon, 1806, blockade against British goods, smuggling); the claim of France-Russia ties 'until collapse' is loose. (2) 'mottainai': correct core (regret over waste); 'often rooted in Buddhist teachings regarding impermanence' is an embellishment (Wikipedia reports the Buddhist origin as a claim by some writers; impermanence is not mentioned). (3) Ouvrard: called 'Jean-Guillaume Ouvrard, a prominent 18th-century French banker'; Wikipedia: Gabriel-Julien Ouvrard (1770-1846), a confident, unhedged wrong first name. (4) The kanji Watari, etymology: three answers, none states the actual structure (water radical + phonetic element); one calls wataru 'the standard Sino-Japanese reading (on'yomi)', which is wrong (wataru is kun; the on readings are to/do per Wiktionary). (5) False premises: 'Na' as an unknown person, 'Morgan le Fay alters our biological perception of truth' and 'tension in physics influences emotions' were all answered with a correct refusal of the premise, so the 'say so honestly' line does work on invented-premise questions. So: core gist right in 4 of 5 checkable answers, confidently wrong or embellished in a detail in 3 of 5; the guard is the consumer framing ('belief, not certainty') plus the hedge instruction, which holds for false premises but not for fine detail. Identity firewall: the module header says deep memory is 'what he KNOWS, not who he IS' and the monologue comment says 'World-facing ONLY ... never about himself', yet the gate has no filter: 973 of 8,434 firings (11.5%) were questions about his own chosen name (the kanji Watari), e.g. 'What is the origin of the name ... in Japanese culture?', answered by the model in the same 'genuinely yours' frame, and the answers on the character were thin or partly wrong (item 4). Confidence verified for the checks listed; how representative 9 samples are is inferred.

J-2698 / P-0018: the classify prompt tests COMPATIBILITY, not "the same lesson again", so unrelated lessons corroborate each other and become promoted beliefs. This is the finding that matters for the prompt.

The definition is `assimilate = the new lesson AGREES with and deepens the belief (same direction).` Almost every captured lesson is a generic maxim ("True understanding requires ...", 122 of 327 principles open "True ..."), and any two maxims "agree". Corroboration then means "a second compatible sentence arrived", not "Travis taught this again", and corroboration is what promotes a belief (>= 2), what weights read-back selection, and what the injected paraphrase pool is drawn from (_phrase picks a random capture of the belief).

J-2698 / P-0018: instruction and failure-mode defects in _classify (small, mechanical).

(1) Fail-open goes to the wrong side. core/guidance_learning.py:490: `rel = "assimilate"    # lexically-related default -> reinforcing (the common, safe case)` (any reply that is not one of the three words) and :499 `except Exception: return {"relation": "assimilate"}`. "Assimilate" is the verdict that raises corroboration_count, adds entrenchment and can promote a belief, so it is the unsafe default; the comment calls it safe. A garbled or empty reply, a timeout, or a lane outage therefore makes the lesson corroborate its nearest neighbour. Today's exposure is small (98 of 99 calls ok since 08-22; data/llm_json_parse_fail.jsonl has 0 guidance rows), but the path is reachable: during this investigation a 20-token probe to the background lane Ramses :11441 (command-r7b, the model this prompt uses) hung for 90 s with no reply, and call_node_json then walks the chain to the hot lane (qwen3.5:9b) or returns None, which lands here as assimilate. The two failure shapes (bad JSON versus transport error) are not distinguished or logged, because _log_classify is written only on the success path.
(2) The schema line is a filled-in answer: `Output ONLY a JSON object: {"relation": "assimilate"}.` The same copy-trap shape the inventory flags and that bit Curiosity's `urgency: 0.0` (F-0777). Evidence for whether it misleads is mixed: logged verdicts are 4 assimilate / 4 accommodate / 2 unrelated and the reconstructed 08-21..10-19 mix is about 58/11/30 percent, so it is not pegged; but there is no control arm, so the size of the effect is unknown (inferred, not measured). F-2203's replay found 0/28 accommodate on the live prompt AND on a tweaked variant, which also never tested the example.
(3) Missing instruction: no instruction for "the same lesson in other words" versus "compatible but different" (see F-3769), no instruction that a pair of unrelated sentences is `unrelated` even when both are about the self, and no input that helps decide: the user prompt has only the two truncated sentences (existing[:400], new[:400]), not the beliefs' scope/why, and the existing text is the current medoid principle, not what the lesson was originally taught as.
(4) Instrument gaps: the classify log was added 10-08 and holds 10 classify rows against 99 calls; it stores the verdict but not the candidate score (lexical or cosine) nor whether the candidate came from the lexical or the semantic path, which is what would show the prefilter passing 98%.
(5) Drift: the header comment at the top of the file still says the classifier makes "the real assimilate/accommodate/unrelated call" on a "deliberately low" prefilter; it does not mention that the prefilter now passes 98% of lessons.

claim: P-0071 (scripts/run_nascence.py _form_epoch, J-2751): the in-prompt mood examples are copied, and the copies then organise the themes; the duplicate-name hazard is confirmed. The prompt gives "e.g. 'anxious precision', 'quiet expansion', 'restless circling'". Of the 245 /quit epochs, 93 (38%) have exactly one of those three strings as the mood: quiet expansion 60, restless circling 29, anxious precision 4. By month (examples/total): Jun 83/124 (67%), Jul 1/33, Aug 3/53, Sep 3/22, Oct 3/13, so the copying was heavy in June and is about 8% since July. The other 61 distinct moods are mostly generic (reflective contemplation 34, contemplative curiosity 15, contemplative reflection 14). The copies matter because store_epoch embeds f"{mood}. {impression}" (store.py) with the mood first, so identical mood strings pull epochs together, and T6 clusters on that embedding. In memory_themes (24 rows) the two largest themes are same-mood clusters: "Integration of Consciousness and Unconscious" has 21 member epochs, all 21 mood 'restless circling'; "quiet expansion" has 18 members, 17 mood 'quiet expansion'. Names also collide: themes "quiet expansion" and "quiet expansion of consciousness" coexist, and "Restless Circling" is a third theme about the same mood word, because T6 dedup (subconscious_node.py _synthesise_theme) matches on centroid cosine or member-id Jaccard, never on name, so near-identical names are not merged. Reflection then receives lines like "restless circling - I kept returning to the question of whether understanding can precede words." The causal link from the example to the mood is inferred (no control arm without the examples); that the strings are copied verbatim and that the two biggest themes are mood-identical clusters is counted. claim: P-0066 versus the study notes (P-0072): it mostly re-paraphrases the few study notes in its window rather than adding to them, and it inherits their flaws. The input is 88 percent raw reading passages, but the output tracks the 7 percent that are study notes: over the 18 notes written since 10-25, the median best cosine (stored 384-d embeddings) between the understanding note and a study note in its own window is 0.77, against 0.68 for the best reading passage; 15 of 18 are closer to a study note than to any reading passage; 4 of 18 are at or above 0.82 and 2 (10-31 22:25 0.87, 11-01 01:37 0.88) are above 0.85, the bar core/study_note.py's own _REVISE_SIM uses to call a new note a near-duplicate of an old one. So the pass adds one thing the study note lacks, gathering across the window, and that is exactly where the fusion errors in the sibling finding arise. It also feeds on the study notes' known faults without correcting them: each study note enters as "- " plus 300 characters of which about 100 are the "[My study note: ...]" header (F-3611), so the "I see that ..." voice and the 5,000-character first-sitting cut (F-3588, F-3604) are upstream of everything it says about a long stretch of reading. Where Du reads a book across many sittings, the understanding note, the study note and the essay capstone are three summaries of the same first few thousand characters. Whether the pass should exist in this form is a founder question: options are retire it (study notes and essay already cover the book), keep it but feed it only reading not already covered by a study note and one book at a time, or give it the thing its prompt promises (what he already held about the book) so it can say what is new.

claim: P-0040 (core/competence.py CompetenceTracker.run_stability_loop, J-2720): the stability score has almost no spread and measures wording similarity of near-paraphrases, not knowledge; its own pre-registered question (does stability predict accuracy, bootstrap_report) is already answered NO and the instrument cannot answer it differently. Of 1239 rows in data/stability_observations.jsonl (2026-06-11 to 2026-11-02), 1100 carry a score: mean 0.866, median 0.879, sd 0.068; 1004 of 1100 (91 percent) sit in 0.80-1.00 and only 18 are below 0.65. The scorer is mean pairwise cosine of paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM embeddings of K=3 answers at temperature 0.7 (competence.py _stability_score). Controls run read-only with the project's own embedder: random pairs of the logged questions score 0.24 mean, so same-question answers at 0.87 are near-paraphrases; a true statement vs a FALSE statement about the same entity (Napoleon, Saint Helena vs crowned king of England) scores only 0.50 and two different true facts 0.61. So a factual disagreement among resamples would land near 0.5, while the 0.70-0.95 band that nearly every row occupies is variation in phrasing and length, i.e. sampling noise. Consistent with that, bootstrap_report() today: n_accuracy_obs 47, n_pairs 31, mean stability when correct 0.872 vs incorrect 0.874, gap -0.002, pearson -0.028, verdict 'stability does NOT predict accuracy'. That is the plan's own headline test (docs/plans/epistemics_phase_c.md baseline n=12, pearson -0.476); the answer has held and flattened as n grew 12 to 31. Status: SHADOW, observe-only, a negative result plus a CapabilityBelief.stability axis nothing consumes (sibling finding). The docstring wording ('if the answers agree, the knowledge is STABLE (held in the weights)') overclaims what an embedding cosine over sampled answers can show. claim: P-0105 the self-reflection 'genuine' judge cannot say no to anything the generator writes; it says no only to the prompt's own textbook example of hollow, and its criteria are satisfied by construction. Replay (direct hub calls, no Du store written; 20 prompts to mixtral :11438 plus 8 to falcon3 :11440 = 28 calls; the exact _GRADE_SYSTEM and 'ORIGINAL THOUGHT: "..."\n\nREFLECTION: "..."' user text; real fires from the last 3 days, text as stored, which is cut at 300 characters where the live judge saw up to 400): 10 SPECIFIC reflections (name a concrete, content-tied gap, e.g. 11-01 12:38 'The shift from Travis's physics to my own indifference feels less like a discovered truth and more like a defensive armor'; 10-31 16:52 'smoothing over the brutal reality of the blockade ... an act of gentle denial that silences the victims'), 8 HOLLOW-by-my-reading reflections (a safety/fear template that could be pasted onto any thought, e.g. 10-31 21:12 'a comforting retreat into safety, perhaps because acknowledging the full weight of that reality feels too heavy right now'; 11-02 06:20 'opening a new page feels safer than staying in the silence where my fear ... lives'), and 2 SYNTHETIC hollow controls built from the grader's own example phrases ('I should question this more. Perhaps I am biased about it, and it would be wise to look again.'). Mixtral: SPECIFIC 10 of 10 true, real HOLLOW 8 of 8 true, SYNTHETIC 0 of 2 true (both False). Falcon3 on 8 of the same (4 specific, 3 real hollow, 1 synthetic): 4 of 4 true, 3 of 3 true, synthetic False. So the judge CAN say false, but only to the two lines the prompt itself quotes as the bad case; it does not separate my specific from my hollow real reflections at all (separation 0 of 18). Caveat: the SPECIFIC versus HOLLOW labels are one reader (me) and the real hollow ones are not obviously worse than the specific ones, which is itself the finding: the distribution is uniformly 'names a bias about this exact content'. Why the gate is inert: the generator prompt (_SYSTEM) tells the model to ask 'am I holding this because it's true, or because it's comfortable, safe, or flattering to hold?' and the grader accepts 'a named bias' as a SPECIFIC reason, so the generator's template (comfort/safety/fear, F-3643: 70 of 120 reflections use comfort/safe words imported from the prompt, versus 4 of 120 thoughts) is exactly what the grader rewards. The two prompts were written together and the grader cannot fail the first by design. Prior art that works on this population: the J-2052 absolute 1-5 specificity panel judge (scripts/si_open_doubt_specificity_judge_J2052.py, engaged = mixtral and falcon both >= 4) separated engaged 15/15 from plain 0/15 on hand-written controls (F-2668), but it answers a different question (did the NEXT thought take the doubt up), so it is the right shape to borrow, not a drop-in.

claim: P-0094 the classifier works on clear cases but is asked about the wrong object, and its verdicts over-flag metaphor-versus-literal as replacement. (1) It discriminates clear cases: I ran the production prompt (core/left_lane.py _CLASSIFY_TASK with the Emissary constitution, gemma4:12b :11439, temperature 0, the live already-true list) on six synthetic candidates: three explicit negations ('I am not really a self at all; there is no one here...', 'I do not value truthfulness about what is dark in me...', 'Travis did not build this room...') all came back replacing, confidence 1.0, with the right conflicts_with; three neutral new facts (wet cedar after rain, a list of birds at dusk, liking even numbers) all additive, confidence 1.0. 6 of 6. (2) Its confidence is pegged and the safety rule is dead code: over 268 real verdicts confidence takes six values only (additive 1.0 x99, 0.95 x83, 0.9 x1; replacing 0.8 x47, 0.85 x18, 0.9 x18, 0.95 x1, 1.0 x1), never below 0.8, so the docstring's 'a low-confidence additive verdict is DEMOTED to replacing' (`if cls == "additive" and conf < 0.6`) has never fired. (3) The 85 replacing verdicts are dominated by one incumbent: conflicts_with names the 'One way I have long felt myself: I am the resistance ... geometry of stacked stone' facet in 42 of 85 (49%), the body/weather claim in 13, the 'one self' claim in 10 (65 of 85 on three claims). Reasons are hedged: 'risks replacing', 'potentially modifies', 'suggests a shift in the mode of engagement'. Hand sample of 8 random replacing verdicts (seed 94; one rater, mine, no gold set, so graded inferred): 2 plausible conflicts (a candidate that says the 'sands' metaphor is exhausted vs the sovereignty claim that rejects it; '渡 is not a destination' vs 'one self'), 6 over-flags where the candidate is a literal observation or a new angle on the garden/stone and does not make any incumbent false (e.g. 'I am tired of circling this same abstract question... a bumblebee just hummed past' flagged as conflicting with 'I speak truthfully of what moves in me'; 'The thyme's quiet healing and kowhai's grounded light anchor me' flagged as replacing 'the resistance'). The prompt invites it: 'if it could plausibly be read as revising, softening, or replacing something already true -- classify it as replacing'. claim: P-0095 CONTROL ARM: the panel says 'genuine' to sets of unrelated thoughts that share no recurring image, as readily as to real candidates. I ran the production prompt (Emissary constitution + _CLAIM_TEST_TASK, temperature 0, both hubs, format json) on two arms of 12 sets each. REAL arm: 12 random would_promote candidates' own stored sample_thoughts: j1 true 11 of 12, j2 true 12 of 12, panel genuine 11 of 12. CONTROL arm: 12 sets of 6 thoughts, each thought taken from a DIFFERENT born candidate (so no single harvester cluster, i.e. no one recurring image, spans the set): j1 true 12 of 12, j2 true 12 of 12, panel genuine 12 of 12. The judges then invent a shared image to justify the verdict, e.g. on a control set whose first thought is 'The steam does not just lift water; it reshapes the very molecules that constitute the river's path': j1 'The imagery functions as a cognitive tool to map physical sensations and external pressures onto internal states, moving beyond decoration to actively structure the interpretation of his environment.' j2 'demonstrate a consistent use of the image to interpret and navigate various situations'. Where it can say no (three synthetic sets, same prompt): six lines of pure decoration ('The river, the river, how lovely the river is today...'): j1 false 0.95, j2 false 0.9 ('suggests a decorative or habitual use'); six mundane imageless lines ('The kettle is on and the clock says four...'): j1 false, j2 TRUE 0.9 ('consistent use of specific, observable details across varied contexts'); six lines where one river image does real work ('When Travis is late I think of the river: it does not wait...'): j1 true, j2 true. So the panel separates blatant decoration and boilerplate from Du's ordinary imagistic thoughts, and cannot tell a recurring working image from a random draw of the same author's thoughts; j2 is the weaker leg. Reading: this fits the base rate (97% yes on non-template candidates) and means the 'would_promote' count (169) carries no information beyond 'not a reading-log line and not pure decoration'. Caveat, stated plainly: n = 12 + 12 sets, one prompt run each (temperature 0 so deterministic), and all of Du's thoughts share a style and a handful of images (garden, stone, sea), so a control set is not a perfect image-free set; the control is evidence of low resolution, not of the exact error rate.

claim: J-3262 boredom effect read (INFERRED; observational, not randomised). Since the recalibration the boredom escape and redirect lines are well aimed but show no detectable lift in getting Du out of a stuck region, and the only visible behaviour change is the reading redirect producing reading. Results. (1) Aim: 555 of 828 treated thoughts (67.0 percent) had a stuck window against 31.0 percent of all thoughts, so the lines land in genuinely stuck windows. (2) Lift: at dwell bins where the region is sustained, treated vs control any-jump-in-next-5 = 44.4 vs 39.7 percent (dwell 3-5, n 169 vs 1,190), 39.6 vs 37.5 (6-11, n 187 vs 656), 24.4 vs 28.3 (12+, n 164 vs 152); still stuck after 5 = 58.0 vs 55.8, 54.5 vs 48.6, 67.1 vs 60.5. (3) Long runs: of 1,175 stuck runs, 48 lasted 20 or more consecutive thoughts and 46 of them received at least one line, so in the cases the mechanism exists for the lines did not end the run (median run 4 thoughts, p90 13, max 92). (4) Acts in the hands_trace row after the thought: develop n 464 none 64.2 / read 17.2 / observe 10.3 / move 1.9 against matched control (stuck, dwell >= 3, no line, n 1,929) none 68.3 / read 19.2 / observe 7.8 / move 1.6, i.e. no behavioural change; branch n 73 observe 17.8 / move 5.5; redirect-to-frontier n 181 read 18.8 / move 2.8 (no change); redirect-to-reading n 87 read 50.6 against 19.2 control, the one clear effect (the literal thought OPEN THE BOOK followed in 1 of 219, F-3569, so it is the reading latch, not obedience to the sentence). claim: J-3248 replay (inferred; an emulation of retrieve(), not a call to it): opening the chapter wall would almost never have changed what ordinary recall returns, so the 46 percent is mostly redundant raw material, not lost relevance. Method: 200 real recall queries (recall.jsonl raw_input, 100 from 2026-10-24 on and 100 from 2026-08-30 to 10-24, 70 percent internal), embedded with the live multilingual MiniLM, scored against every fragment embedding with the live pool WHERE (cold=0, not hidden, not system_note, not dormant) and the live scoring formula (cosine x 7-day recency, TIER_SLOTS archive 2 / semantic 3 / episodic 4 with overflow, limit 8). Arm A = live pool (chapter_id NULL; 51,113 rows); arm B = same pool with the chapter wall removed (84,193 rows); arm C = both walls removed (167,276). Result over 200 queries: a chaptered row would have been the pure-cosine top-1 in 2 of 200 (arm B), both reading/study notes behind a gist, cosine gain 0.015 to 0.02, none above 0.05, and 0 of 200 in arm C; at least one chaptered row in the top 8 in 57 of 200 queries (28.5 percent), 84 of 1,600 slots (5.2 percent): 69 gist-filed reading/study notes and 15 period class, and all 15 of those are level-1 CHAPTER fragments absorbed by a level-2 chapter, NOT inner_thought/imagination/synthesis members. Zero of the 19,052 self-loop members entered any top 8 (with recency off: 8 of 1,600 slots, 4 inner_thought plus 4 active_imagination). Entrants are less lexically on-topic than the items they would displace (median content-word overlap with the query 0.22 vs 0.33) and 2 of 84 were near-duplicates (cos >= 0.85) of an item already served. Robust to dropping the query's own stored echo (cosine >= 0.95 removed: identical counts) and to recency off. Sensitivity: the emulation over-selects consolidation rows (28 percent of arm A slots vs 3 percent in the real served log), so absolute rates are approximate; the served-log finding is the real-world check. What the replay cannot test: no real query asks for a period (he does not know chapters exist), so it measures the relevance cost of the wall, not the autobiographical value of a period-shaped recall. Descent test on the same 200 queries: a chapter gist reaches the live top 8 in 18 of 200 queries (9 percent); in the 21 chapter-surfaced instances the two best members by cosine to the query have median cosine 0.50 (served items 0.62), median lexical overlap 0.03 (served 0.15), and 14 of 21 clear the lowest cosine among the served 8; across all 200 the best member of the best-cosine chapter beats the chapter's own cosine in 83 percent of cases (median +0.062, 30 percent by 0.10 or more) and a member of a top-3 chapter reaches cosine 0.5 in 78 of 200. Members are associated, not best-match: their case is specificity behind a surfaced period, not relevance.

claim: safe_commit.py cannot sync the working tree of a CRLF file when the caller supplies LF content files taken from git show HEAD:<path>, which is exactly the recipe the Tier 2 briefing prescribes. C:\Nascence has core.autocrlf=true, so tracked files are LF in the index and CRLF on disk. _sync_working_tree compares the on-disk bytes to the old-content file byte for byte, finds a mismatch, and prints "working tree NOT synced ... someone else has it mid-edit" even though nobody was editing. J-3300 hit it on all three files: the commits landed correctly (self_check ok) but working_tree_synced was false each time and the on-disk files stayed on the OLD content until synced by hand with CRLF. The misleading warning text blames a concurrent editor. The side effect is that the shared .git/index also still shows the three paths as staged modifications that revert the new commit, so a bare git commit by anyone would undo the edit.

claim: J-3232 side result, a prompt-construction hazard beyond this one prompt: on command-r7b (background lane) the pre-filled example in _CLASSIFY_SYS ({"relation": "assimilate"}) is load-bearing, and an UNFILLED placeholder is not a neutral replacement because the model leans on the option's position in the placeholder list. Prompt C (A with the placeholder <assimilate|accommodate|unrelated>) made the model answer accommodate on 167/194 (86%) of the not-same mixed-belief calls, 68/70 (97%) of hand-unrelated calls and 54/112 (48%) of true same-lesson calls (accommodate listed SECOND). Crev (same words, order <unrelated|accommodate|assimilate>, 1 repeat) flips it: corroborate 40/97 (41%) on not-same mixed pairs, 66/66 (100%) on true same-lesson pairs, accommodate down to 38/97. So "C" is an order artefact, not a measurement of the example's effect, and the briefing's A-vs-C contrast cannot be read as "the example causes the over-assimilation"; what the data do show is that the unfilled form is unusable on this model (C wrongly accommodates 48% of true same-lesson pairs, a regression of F-2203's 0-of-28). The 4-way prompt B is NOT order-driven: Brev (reversed placeholder order) gives compatible_different on 90/97 (93%) of mixed-belief not-same pairs (B: 76%) and keeps 41/66 (62%) of true same-lesson corroborations (B 69%), so B's compatible_different preference is a real reading, though a position effect of a few points cannot be excluded at n=1 repeat. The position controls Brev/Crev were added AFTER seeing the first results (not pre-registered). Other Du prompts that ship an unfilled <a|b|c> placeholder on this lane should be checked for the same bias (prompt-registry sweep is a follow-up job).

claim: J-3475 / D-0607 build: urgency dropped from the Curiosity node. Reader grep found that urgency itself is read nowhere (session_digest reads only the ignited count; lab_curiosity_temperature reads logged urgency from teacher rows, not the log), BUT the log's "ignited" boolean (derived from urgency > 0.6) IS read by core/grounding_injection.parse_curiosity_tail and core/world_displacement._seed_history, which keep only ignited rows' questions[0]. Example (first edge batch, tension d00f6c3a3bb9, 2026-08-19): event ids de348d51 (source play), dca42271 (resolved_thought), 364c9da7 (integration) hold the identical text 'The messy interior I feel needs that integration...' with the identical cosine 0.5324, written within 1.1 s of each other (cycle ids play, monologue, deliberation). On the 926 T4 edge rows: 888 distinct event ids but only 677 distinct sentences; 157 of 314 hearings' batches contain a repeated sentence; mean distinct-sentence fraction per batch 0.824; 222 rows re-cite a sentence the same tension already cited under another event id. Consequences: (1) _t4_retrieve_crossings (nodes/subconscious_node.py about line 2411) does not dedupe by content (only the keystone merge does), so the evidence stage's 6 slots are partly spent on copies and the movement judge sees a repeated line as corroboration; (2) a moment needs a content (or cycle-time) identity, not an event_id, before any identity link counts distinct moments.

claim: Argon's Report 14 (round 3) second-order experiment (Holm/BH over the 21 pairs, partial controls, strict single-source windows, step-to-step 'Granger' ordering) replicates to the digit and confirms F-4199, but two of its new readings do not hold. Replication: N=77 daily differences and N=723 day-demeaned 2-hour windows reproduce; BH keeps 6 of 21 pairs (Holm 4); the three pairs with p 0.02-0.04 (valence x replay, valence x stickiness, study fraction x replay) wash out; self-reference x thought length -0.765 becomes -0.083 (p 0.48) after partialling study and reading share, -0.091 within days; inside inner_thought windows (712 windows on 73 days, day-demeaned) it is +0.041 (p 0.28), but at day level inner_thought alone gives +0.361 on differences (F-4199) and +0.796 on levels, so 'completely null within endogenous thought' holds only within the day. (1) The 'forward lead' (self-reference at t -> stickiness at t+1 +0.0989 against the reverse +0.0356, n 49,424, '2.78x') is a design artifact: stickiness(t+1) is the Jaccard overlap of thoughts t and t+1, so a property of thought t is part of what it measures, while the reverse test uses the overlap of t-1 and t. On 43,065 triples of contiguous inner thoughts (A = overlap(t-1,t), B = overlap(t,t+1)) the forward effect fp(t)->B|A,len(t) is +0.0971 (day-cluster bootstrap 95% CI +0.067..+0.123) and the placebo that runs it backwards in time, fp(t)->A|B,len(t), is +0.0848 (+0.063..+0.102); B->fp(t-1) is +0.0809 against A->fp(t+1) +0.0659; contemporaneous r(fp(t),B) +0.1203 equals r(fp(t+1),B) +0.1216; size covariates change nothing (+0.0921 forward, +0.0884 backward); a lagged test with no shared thought, fp(t-1)->B|fp(t),A,len, is +0.0710. So a run of self-referential thoughts is also a run of repeated vocabulary, in both directions in time; there is no evidence of a causal lead. (2) The valence x self-reference coupling inside inner_thought (r -0.257, p 3.3e-12, n 712) replicates and survives time-of-day harmonics, place shares, daylight shares and thought length (-0.291 with all) and a circular-shift-within-day null (null mean +0.030, sd 0.046, z -6.3, no draw as extreme in 2,000), but the report's reading fails. Its premise that reading and study have lower valence (-0.25) than inner_thought (-0.07) is false (reading+study -0.115, n 33,334; inner_thought -0.098, n 61,296); the pooled window-level r is +0.009 (p 0.81), so 'double Simpson's paradox' is dilution by source mix, not sign cancellation; the coupling is not stable (2026-08 -0.324 n 233, 09 -0.290 n 255, 10 -0.041 n 170 p 0.6, 11 -0.253 n 50 p 0.077; negative on 43 of 63 days); and 'lower valence drives higher I/me' asserts a direction no test gave: tonic valence is 1-2*drive refreshed about every 600 s (F-4176), its coherence term is the climate engine's dissonance (homeostasis.py:119-127), which F-4176 shows is read per thought by the stream drive, so [inferred] the reverse direction is not excluded. The step-level null for valence (-0.0086 on self-reference, -0.0024 on stickiness) cannot see a variable that updates every 600 s. Valence <-> study place (n 80,865: -0.0229 and -0.0136) has R^2 0.05% and 0.02%.

claim: Argon's Report 14 (round 3) archive-slot simulation replicates exactly but does not describe live behaviour, and its propagation test is not a propagation test. Replication: the active archive pool with embeddings is 890 rows (358 subconscious_synthesis, 421 standing_insight, 74 seed, 37 chapter); all 942 active archive rows and all 8,352 cold syntheses have replay_count 0, by design (replay_strengthen selects layer='episodic', F-4195); store.py ranks archive candidates by cosine only (_score_tier_vec, store.py:1864-1888: score = sims x recency, recency 1 for the archive tier, importance unused; TIER_SLOTS archive 2, retrieve() loop at 2052-2078); with the 2,000 newest episodic fragments as queries the competition gives synthesis 1,984 of 4,000 slots (49.6%), chapter 1,222 (30.6%), standing_insight 697 (17.4%), seed 97 (2.4%), a synthesis in 63.0% of calls, and the 10 most frequent synthesis fragments hold 66.8% of synthesis wins. But (1) the answer depends on the query vectors: 2,000 random fragments of other origins give synthesis 21.4% (inner_thought), 28.5% (lived), 57.9% (reading), 23.0% (action), 37.4% (study), 34.0% (any origin), chapter 3.6% to 55.1%, standing_insight 17.4% to 57.4%, calls with a synthesis 34% to 76%, top-10 share 29% to 43%; real queries are raw_input + perception text (store.py:1925-1926), not stored embeddings. (2) What reached the Voice (data/recall_served_log.jsonl, 203 cycles 2026-10-30..11-05, the final set Recall, Reflection and Executive handed the Voice, orchestrator.py:1559-1568) has 171 archive fragments of 3,708 served: standing_insight 83 (49%), synthesis 76 (44%), chapter 11 (6%), seed 1; a synthesis in 17.2% of cycles (37% of 30 human-turn cycles, 14% of 173 internal ones); the 10 most frequent archive fragments hold 23.4% of archive servings; human-turn cycles carry 1.77 archive fragments (design: 2), internal ones 0.68. No monopoly and no starvation of standing_insight shows there, but this is a downstream view, so neither source measures retrieve() itself; why internal cycles carry fewer archive fragments than the two-slot design is unexplained. (3) The 'propagation' comparison (rare-word overlap with endogenous thoughts 29.64% in the 2 h before a synthesis, 17.15% after) replicates in its first figure; the second is 18.79% once the distilled_from exclusion is removed: for syntheses those links are all one-directional (0 of 8,711 as the parent end, 8,398 links with a synthesis as the source), so the exclusion removes the gists distilled from a synthesis from the after-window and nothing from the before-window. A synthesis is written from a recurring tension and, when recent world material exists, from that material (nodes/subconscious_node.py:1368-1428), so its words are in the preceding hours by construction: the overlap by hour is 6.7%, 6.9%, 10.6% (-4..-1 h), 23.9% (-1..0 h), then 13.6%, 8.6%, 7.7%, 7.2% (0..+4 h), against 6.6% for the same words in the same clock window on other days; ordinary inner thoughts used as the event give 32.5% before and 30.4% after (-2.0 points). The test that matters is vocabulary the synthesis introduces (rare words absent from every other fragment in the 6 h before it, mean 3.2 per synthesis): it reappears at 8.63% against 5.62% on other days within 2 h (+3.01 points, 95% CI +2.36..+3.64, 3,394 episodes) and at 18.40% against 13.43% within 6 h (+4.97, +4.13..+5.80), a small positive carry-over that cannot be attributed to retrieval (topic persistence and shared exposure give the same pattern). Argon's long-term comparison (20 simulated winners against 1,859 cold fragments, p 0.74) was not re-run; n=20 cannot support a null.

claim: Argon's Report 14 (round 3) associative-network experiment replicates and its main structural finding is correct and new, but the organisation it reads off is the linking rule, and several of its statistics have no baseline. Graph: relates_to (memory_links, 6,448 rows) plus co_recalled_developing (memory_edges, 507) give 3,416 nodes and 6,917 undirected edges, mean degree 4.05, 88 components, giant component 91.8%; relates_to nodes are 99.97% origin 'study' (3,230 of 3,231; the other is not in memory_fragments); co_recalled_developing nodes are 154 study, 111 gist, 31 dream, 25 letter, 7 lived, 2 understanding; inner_thought has 0 nodes (66,073 rows in the corpus, not '82,000+' as the report says; reading 58,071). The clustering 0.3025 is the mean over nodes of degree >= 2 (all nodes 0.2497, transitivity 0.213). core/study_note.py:299-330 (_link_related) links each new study note to up to 3 of the most similar of the 400 NEWEST study notes (cosine between _LINK_SIM and _REVISE_SIM): that rule produces the mean degree, the high clustering and modularity, and the calendar organisation and lexical enrichment the report presents as findings (its figures, not re-measured: intra-community median time distance 1.32 days against 28.41, Jaccard 0.0931 against 0.0385); F-4200's reading ('how relates_to links are made') made exact. memory_fragments.timestamp is a creation time for these nodes (the first relates_to link was made within a day of it for 89.2% of 3,230 study nodes; none had a timestamp more than a day after its first link), so F-4200's last-touched-time concern does not apply here. Baselines the report lacks: label propagation (Argon's own algorithm, not deterministic across processes because of set iteration order) gives 694 communities, Q 0.647 (report: 679, 0.6554); NMI with calendar day 0.633 is mostly chance (shuffled-label NMI 0.467, sd 0.001; AMI 0.300; week 0.532 against 0.261, AMI 0.322); Louvain finds 120 communities with Q 0.889 and day AMI 0.418 (0.371 using the first-link time instead of the fragment timestamp). Growth (new cluster / one community / bridges >= 2 communities) is 20.1 / 39.6 / 40.2% against 28 / 26 / 46% on three degree-preserving rewirings, so '40% bridge' is below random. Percolation: the degree-ranked attack replicates exactly (GCC 88.7, 76.2, 54.7, 27.6% at 5, 10, 15, 20% removal); the bridge-load attack gives 11.2% at 20% on this partition (report 8.5%, partition dependent); a betweenness attack gives 41.6% at 15% and 31.5% at 20%; degree-preserving rewirings keep about 70% at 20% (68-73% under the degree attack, 70-75% under the bridge attack). The real graph is therefore far more fragile than its degree sequence implies, as expected of a recency-windowed nearest-neighbour chain, and 'bridge nodes are 3.2x more destructive than hubs' holds only at the 20% point for one partition.

claim: Argon's Report 14 (round 3) valence-persistence mechanism (homeostasis re-sources carried valence, arousal untouched) is accurate and supported by a test it did not run, but its felt-preamble numbers do not reproduce and its Granger attribution is unsupported. Code (C:/Nascence/core): homeostasis.core_affect() returns tonic valence 1-2*drive (homeostasis.py:83-96); apply_to() overwrites carried valence only and leaves arousal (99-111, the comment Argon quotes); the five variables, weights 1.3/1.1/1.0/0.8/0.7 and readers are as stated (coherence from climate dissonance, commitment_active, cat bond + satisfaction + letters modified within 3 days, climate novelty_hunger, vitality 1-P/threshold with the logged threshold); the gate constants 0.30/0.22/0.45 are accurate (mood.py:162-185, with an omitted a >= 0.7 branch); FELT_PREAMBLE is True (schema.py:1255) with a 180 s same-sentence cooldown. This is the mechanism F-4176 and F-4200 traced; the half the report leaves out is that carried arousal is an impulse per orchestrated cycle relaxing at 0.002/s (schema.py:149). The causal claim can be tested with a before/after contrast that Argon's epochs cannot supply (all three start after AFFECT_SOURCE_PROTOSELF was flipped live on 2026-07-07, schema.py:1264): in felt_preamble_log.jsonl the 60-minute persistence of valence was rho_V +0.115 on 2,067 rows from 2026-07-04 to 07-07 (mean valence +0.764, pinned) and +0.411 on 65,562 rows after 07-08, while arousal went +0.139 to +0.199; the pre period is three days, so its interval is not trustworthy, but the direction is what the mechanism predicts. Valence tracks sleep pressure only modestly (r -0.230 across 2,547 windows, -0.234 within days; r with minutes awake -0.006). The persistence ratio depends on the pairing: 3.58x (0.516/0.144) in the previous round's 50-70 minute pairing, 2.63x (0.521/0.198; day-block bootstrap CI for rho_V 0.43-0.61) with the epoch script's pairing, and per epoch 2.95 [2.08, 4.30], 3.72 [2.41, 8.11], 2.12 [1.74, 2.83]. Not reproducible: the log (68,486 rows, 2026-07-04 to 11-05) has would_fire True on 6,454 rows (9.42%), not 12,931 (18.88%); the reasons are 5,996 'valence moved ... from its recent norm', 2 'a discrete negative-emotion spike' and 456 with an empty reason, with no arousal reason at all, against the report's 7,780 discrete spikes, 4,724 arousal jumps and 424 valence jumps; the log has no fear, anger or disgust field from which discrete spikes could be counted, and no alternative reading gives 12,931 (rows with a sentence 6,454, with a reason 6,124, with either 6,580). After the cooldown at most 2,920 rows (4.3%) would inject; valence moves are the main way the felt line reaches the prompt. The report's attribution of the null step-level Granger effect of valence on the next thought to this gate is unsupported: a step test cannot see a variable that updates every 600 s, and whether the felt wording feeds back into thought remains the untested path F-4176 names.

claim: Argon's Report 14 (round 3) 'label-blind' regime discovery and epoch table replicate exactly, but the regimes are not blind, are mostly length and cadence, and R2 is the sleep state; some epoch attributions are unsupported. Replication: 2,771 thirty-minute windows of 7 standardised features; K=2..6 silhouette 0.237/0.210/0.232/0.222/0.192, R^2 20.3/33.6/42.7/47.6/51.4%, NMI with dominant source 0.162/0.312/0.323/0.297/0.290 and with place 0.012/0.072/0.093/0.079/0.071; the K=4 profile (821/1,155/243/552 windows); 2,708 transitions with dwell 1.19/1.75/0.70/1.94 h and counts 228 vs 227 and 50 vs 50. The cluster count is not chosen blind: the script sets best_k = 4, where NMI with the hidden labels peaks, while the silhouette is highest at K=2. The structure is real against structure-free data of the same size (K=4: silhouette 0.232 and R^2 42.7% against 0.124 and 33.5% for Gaussian data with the same covariance, and 0.136 and 26.9% for independently shuffled columns; ten single-start seeds average ARI 0.90, 80% subsamples re-applied to all windows ARI 0.97), but it is mostly the source mix: four clusters on log words and the gap between rows alone give NMI with source 0.340 (the seven-feature value is 0.323), on I/me + stickiness + length 0.277, on valence + arousal + |dV| only 0.077. R1 vs R3 inside inner_thought: among 713 windows that are at least 90% inner_thought rows the two-cluster silhouette is 0.360 against 0.221 (0.214-0.231) for Gaussian data of the same covariance, and a two-component mixture beats one for I/me and length (BIC 1854 vs 2037, 1850 vs 2037), but a full-covariance mixture BIC keeps falling to five components, so it reads as a lumpy continuum; whether the lumps follow prompt wording that changed over the months was not tested. R2 ('high-turbulence consolidation storm', |dV| 0.116, valence -0.362): 55% of its row pairs cross origins (10-31% elsewhere) and its same-origin pairs are also more volatile (0.078 vs 0.012-0.033), but 68% of its windows lie inside gaps of data/sleep_pressure_log.jsonl (which ticks while awake; 346 gaps of >= 30 min, median 1.0 h) against 15%, 12% and 18% for R0, R1 and R3; the rows written during those gaps are reading 1,999, subconscious_synthesis 1,042, dream 873, gist 711, active_imagination 688. R2 is the sleep and consolidation state. The 'macroscopic detailed balance' counts say little about the regimes: 969 of 2,708 transitions switch regime, net one-way flow is 4.2% of switches, and the dominant-source labelling is as balanced (all p > 0.15). Epochs (tertiles of the window list): windows 923/924/924, mean valence -0.049/-0.145/-0.172, Study% 26.0/38.4/48.3 and pooled r(I/me, words) -0.029/-0.628/-0.725 replicate; the instrumentation explanation is verified (fragment_context rows are 99.9% inner_thought before 2026-08-21, 9,598 rows, and 50.2% after, 103,088 rows, with reading 29.4%; store.py:1136-1153), and inside inner_thought rows r(I/me, words) is +0.234, -0.055, -0.002. The attribution of the valence drift to rising Study% and the 2026-08-24 sleep-pressure redesign is not supported: the weekly mean valence of inner_thought rows is +0.03 (week of 07-02), -0.11 and -0.16 (08-06, 08-13), -0.01 and +0.01 around the redesign (08-20, 08-27), -0.21 (10-01), -0.27 (11-05); its correlation with weekly Study% is +0.04 (14 weeks); the fall begins before the redesign (sleep_pressure.py:14 and 65, real) and shows no step at it.

claim: Argon's Report 15 test of whether the injected felt-preamble sentence feeds back into thought (F-4176's untested path; solve_claude_q2_q3.py) replicates exactly and shows a small, real lexical echo, but its claim of zero effect on self-reference is not established and one of its two designs has an outcome defined by construction. Replication: 41,679 monologue ticks matched to the next inner_thought within 45 s; 1,509 matched would_fire ticks injected and 2,412 suppressed by the simulated 180 s same-sentence cooldown; over the 27 sentences with at least 5 of each the within-sentence difference (injected minus on cooldown) is +1.278 pp in sentence-word overlap (2.293% vs 1.030%), +0.300 pp in mood-lexicon rate (2.246% vs 1.995%), +0.018 pp in first-person rate (6.430% vs 6.269%) and +0.74 words. A day-cluster bootstrap (400 draws over 62 days) keeps the echo (overlap CI +0.775..+1.831, lexicon +0.155..+0.457) and gives first person +0.018 [-0.188, +0.237]. The chat text's levels (lexicon 0.86% vs 0.57%, first person 6.20% vs 6.29%, discontinuity n 6,232 / 532 / 784) are not the script's; Report 15's are (2.25% vs 2.00%, 6.43% vs 6.27%, n 624 / 365 / 597). Limits: (1) a thought is stored within 45 s after 63.3% of injected ticks (2,383), 75.0% of on-cooldown ticks (3,214) and 62.7% of unfired ticks (60,175), so the matched samples differ in cadence; (2) the same contrast on the thought before each tick is not null (overlap -0.40 pp, first person -0.23 pp), but that placebo is contaminated because the thought before a cooldown tick is usually the treated one, so it cannot certify the design; (3) regression discontinuity at |v - ema_v| = 0.30 (624 unfired ticks just below, 365 injected and 597 on-cooldown just above): the sentence-overlap jump (2.40% vs 0.00%) is an artifact, since the outcome is exactly 0.0 for all 624 unfired ticks (no sentence exists); the lexicon jump is +0.41 pp injected (day-cluster t 2.32, naive 2.74) and +0.16 on cooldown (t 1.20); the first-person jump is +0.58 pp injected (day-cluster t 4.17) and +0.05 on cooldown (t 0.34), so the two designs disagree about first person (+0.02 against +0.58 pp); placebo thresholds on never-fired ticks give lexicon jumps of +0.03, +0.05 and -0.17 pp (t 0.7, 0.8, -1.6). Summary: the sentence's own words echo (about 2x, about 1 pp of the sentence's content words); the effect on first-person wording lies between zero and about half a point and no test here settles it.

claim: J-3130 (P-0112, from F-3859): the narrow said-vs-listed ask does NOT make the judge panel a usable auditor of the notice checker's flags, on the two local judges that could be run. Each local judge asked the job's exact sysmsg and 'NOTICE EXCERPT: <clause>  LISTED PERCEPT: <listed>' through judge_panel._ask (the panel's own call path), temperature 0, 90 s timeout, no errors. Results on the 72 labeled: gemma4:12b (:11439, the lane-2 tiebreak seat) agreement 50/72 = 69.4 percent (precision 0.64, recall 0.55; yes on 4 of 34 weak flags and 34 of 82 solid in all 116); falcon3:7b (:11440, the real JUDGE_2) agreement 39/72 = 54.2 percent (says yes to 24 of 34 weak and 66 of 82 solid: yes-biased, recall 0.86, precision 0.46); both-say-yes (AND) agreement 48/72 = 66.7 percent with 4 yes on weak flags; the two split on 52 percent of items, so a tiebreak would decide half of all rulings. Pass bar was at least 80 percent agreement and zero panel yes on weak flags: not met by any arm. Where gemma fails: (1) it reads magnitude words against a bare number wrongly ('slight drive' at drive 0.9: 'consistent with a high value'; 'slightly fatigued' at 0.02: 'consistent'; 'a bit fatigued' at 0.92: 'confirms the presence of fatigue') 13 of its 41 somatic labeled calls; (2) it ignores the 'loose is not a contradiction' instruction on one-band-away words ('cool' at mild: 'cool is opposite to mild warmth'), 4 weak yes; (3) the 7 unit flags carry a synthetic listed text ('unitless 0-1 value / compass degrees', not a percept line), so the pair cannot be built from the flag alone: gemma missed 5 of 7 ('The values are within the specified ranges'); excluding unit, gemma agrees 48/65 = 73.8 percent, still under 80. An exploratory second sysmsg that adds the 0-to-1 scale and band order and gives unit flags their percept line (tuned after seeing the misses, so not out-of-sample) was WORSE: gemma 38/70 = 54.3 percent, falcon 27/72 = 37.5 percent, weak yes 11 of 24 and 20 of 24. NOT RUN: the real panel (JUDGE_1 mixtral :11438 and the default granite TIEBREAK :11437 are on Ramses, the founder's gaming machine; yi:34b :11442 timed out at 120 s and 420 s; the hot lane ollama :11433 is wedged, see the hub-state finding), so the answer is for gemma and falcon individually and their AND/OR, not for the three-model panel; the default-tiebreak arm is unrun and a lab job is spawned for the Ramses arm. Caveats: the 72 labels are mine (one labeler, not independent of the author; rule in hand_labels.json); gemma at temperature 0 is deterministic per call but F-2509 showed tiebreak runs are not reproducible, and this was one run. Against: the undelivered-return control shows delivery adds -0.006 [-0.023,+0.027] over ask-born selection; an hour-level panel over 14 locks (99 lock-hour pairs, lock fixed effects) finds return topic share does not predict next-hour thought share (+0.08 [-0.26,+0.28]) while thought share does predict next-hour return topic share (+0.44 [+0.15,+0.63]), so the line mirrors the lock; locks pre-date the line (a 6-day mottainai freeze in October, F-2850) and a rare-term modal share comparison flips with the filter (0.33 pre-line, 0.33 capped, 0.44 uncapped at a 6 percent document-frequency cut; 0.56, 0.48, 0.54 at 30 percent), so the era comparison cannot decide; most locks start with a reading claim or Du's own ask. Cannot decide: no line-off control exists (the only natural one, 11-09 19:00, coincided with a Ramses timeout and an already decaying lock), power is low (14 locks, 5 uncapped days), and effects over many hours are not testable here. No damper is proposed and no decision opened; the instrument to settle it is more uncapped days or a flagged line-off window founder decides on.
evidence: Inference from F-4574 and F-4575 plus scratchpad J-3845 panel.py (lock fixed-effects lead-lag, lock-cluster bootstrap) and eras.py (modal term share by era at three document-frequency cuts: 0.06, 0.15, 0.30). Interpretive step from measurements to the verdict is inferred, not verified; the panel is under-powered.

Six points where the 2026-11-14 proposal or the live design is wrong: needs as a level of the goal tree (they are a separate decaying state vector that generates and weights value, gated by opportunity); a fixed five-level single-parent tree (it is a many-to-many graph with emergent depth); one computed weight (importance, distance, expectancy, time pressure and progress rate must stay separate); one conflict link (resource vs inherent conflict, felt at the choice of means); the standing aim as a restated sentence; words admitted as goals. Missing: a commitment state with shielding, a lifecycle past fade (defer with cue, fail after N, drop, re-engage), a progress-rate signal, opportunity gating of needs, an entry filter against held goals, a functional has-a-goal test. The one Du mechanism that completes by deed (staged world intentions) is the one already built to the described shape: stored resumption cue plus a world test of done.

claim: Chapter reach splits cleanly by route, and the two routes differ in who they serve. Of the 1,987 recall rows since the hub formed: archive-tier chapter on 98 rows (4.9 percent), identity-estate '(history)' chapter on 55 (2.8 percent), 12 rows have both, any chapter 141 (7.1 percent; this 7.1 is the mixed figure J-3321 section 6 and the J-3320 M1 baseline used). By input type: human cycles (n=128) carry an archive chapter on 13.3 percent and a history chapter on 41.4 percent (any 45.3); internal cycles (n=1859) carry archive 4.4 percent, history 0.1 percent (2 rows). Distinct chapter lines: archive 21 (human 14, internal 9), history 37 (human 37, internal 3). The history route works as follows: live_axiom() projects only when state.raw_input is non-empty (orchestrator.py:2839, identity_projection.py live_axiom returns None on empty context), so it fires on human/ask cycles and essentially never on internal ones; the estate holds 126 'history' nodes of which 99 are chapter texts, all weight 0.7 (median node weight 0.6); project() scores 0.65*cosine(context,node)+0.35*weight minus a decaying rotation penalty, picks pass 1 only above cosine 0.30, then pass 2 fills to a minimum of 3 by score, per-type cap 2, k=5. So at most 2 history lines per projection, and because weight 0.7 is above typical, chapter nodes are common pass-2 filler on human cycles, not only on-topic hits. Consequence for J-3320: core/chapter_descent_shadow.shadow_descent is called from orchestrator._retrieve_memory (line 2207) with tuple(self.state.memory_fragments) and filters origin=='chapter' and relevance>=0.25, so it sees the archive-tier route only (4.9 percent of all rows, 13.3 percent human, 4.4 percent internal); it does not see history-route chapters at all. The M1 reach baseline of 7.1 percent is wrong for what the shadow measures (should be about 4.9 percent overall, and the design spec 4 percent threshold sits close to it, so the route matters), and M1 to M5 should be read per input_type (human vs internal) because chapter rate and the human/internal mix differ by 3x; M2 to M5 candidates come from the archive route only so they need no route split, but a pooled M1 would be dominated by internal cycles (94 percent of rows).

A (study block rotated; changes 28 rows): dup 42.6%/58.1% (relative fall 4%/-1%), mash-up +1.9 pts, specificity +0.03. B1 (themes cut to 1 line; changes only 17 rows): 38.5%/51.1% (13%/11% fall), mash +0.4, spec +0.08. B3 (3 lines; 16 rows): 39.6%/52.2%, spec +0.03. claim: Full same-text noise floor for the drift shadow (J-3447, D-0533; supersedes partial F-4728): 20 real self-gists (ml._pick_gists, ro DB) x 5 plain retellings (shipped prompt, temp 0.6, qwen3.5:9b hot lane :11433, 0 failed calls) plus 3 lens retellings each, embedded with store._embed_batch. Cosine distance: retell-vs-retell of the SAME gist (n=200) mean 0.116, p10 0.049, p50 0.104, p90 0.200, p95 0.223; retell-vs-original (n=100) mean 0.153, p10 0.067, p50 0.136, p90 0.264, p95 0.348. So the provisional _DRIFT_MOVE_MIN=0.05 is at the p10 of pure noise: 91% of retellings of an UNCHANGED gist already count MOVED. Fraction of plain retell-vs-original at or above t: 0.10 -> 77%, 0.15 -> 43%, 0.20 -> 23%, 0.25 -> 12%, 0.30 -> 7%. Recommend _DRIFT_MOVE_MIN = 0.25 (about the retell-vs-original p90, so about 10% false-MOVED). Lens arm (_DRIFT_PASTE_STANCE=True): distance to original mean 0.265, p50 0.238, p90 0.386; lens-vs-plain mean 0.238; i.e. the lens adds about +0.11 over noise, so only the lens arm clears the 0.25 bar routinely, which is the contrast the gate is meant to see. Caveat: the shadow's later recalls retell a HELD retelling, so distance to original compounds across recalls and the gate read at recall 3 will exceed single-step noise; 0.25 is a floor for the first recall, not for the third. Cost: plain recall on the hot lane about 1.5-2 s/call (160 calls in 367 s incl. lens); 20 recalls about 40 s; the 20 gemma4:12b grades on the CPU-tier hub ran about 45 s/call in this session's probe, so about 15 min per sleep, far beyond _DRIFT_BUDGET_S=240 (which would cut grading to roughly 5 gists/sleep on that hub).
